Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly tie-out of the policy administration seriatim extract to the valuation model in-force file; unresolved breaks escalate to the Appointed Actuary before reserves are booked

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 14 (Valuation) Standards 14.2-14.5 on reliable and complete valuation data, read with ICP 8 (Risk Management and Internal Controls) Standard 8.8, and re-read against the local equivalents each entity files under (Solvency II Art. 82 data quality, NAIC VM-31 Section 3.D reliance and data reconciliation, OSFI E-25); re-verified at each quarter-end close

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly Life & Annuity valuation close for every writing entity in the IAIS-supervised group: policy admin seriatim extract, data quality gate, valuation model load, reserve roll-forward and ledger booking

In-scope systems.value: Seriatim extract staged from the policy administration system into the enterprise data warehouse, loaded to the Prophet/Axis valuation run; reserve output posted to the general ledger

Compliance procedure documented.value: Quarterly Reserve Data Reconciliation Procedure — extract specification by product, record-count and amount tie-out, tolerance table by product line, break classification codes, override rules and sign-off ladder

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary; re-approved annually and on any policy administration release that changes the extract schema, product codes or status codes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Reconciliation must close by working day 8 of the quarter-end close, ahead of actuarial reserve sign-off at WD 10 and the entity statutory/QRT submission dates that follow it

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close-calendar tasks fire to the Data Engineer and Valuation Actuary at WD 3 (extract delivered), WD 5 (tie-out complete) and WD 8 (all breaks cleared or accepted)

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed reconciliation report, extract row counts and hash totals, break log and override memos retained 10 years from the valuation date alongside the quarter's actuarial workpapers

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every break above tolerance is raised as a data-quality issue carrying policy count, reserve impact, source system, root cause and the release that fixes it

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs every residual unreconciled difference and every manual override applied to the valuation in-force file before reserves are booked

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All quarterly reserve-data reconciliations performed in the year (four per valuation entity), their seriatim extracts, break logs and the reserve balances booked from them by product line

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Record-count difference must be zero; aggregate reserve difference within 0.05% of gross policy reserves and USD 250k absolute per entity; any unexplained break above tolerance left inside a booked reserve is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly; independent testing re-performs one full quarter per half-year and adds a mandatory retest of every break open for more than one quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Must sit outside the valuation and actuarial data teams and must not have prepared or reviewed the reconciliation under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Reserve-data reconciliation test workpaper (independent extract, tie-out re-performance, break sample, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Valuation / ICP 14

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed quarterly reconciliation reports, the extract-to-model data lineage diagram and the break log, producible to the group-wide supervisor or a local on-site inspection within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Appointed Actuary answers valuation data questions directly; Regulatory Reporting Manager coordinates supervisory-college and local-regulator requests; Chief Actuary clears any reserve restatement before it is disclosed

checklist.step: Freeze the valuation date and the extract specification
actions: Confirm the quarter-end valuation date and cut-off timestamp with the Controller against the published close calendar.
Open the extract specification and confirm the field list, product code list and policy status codes match the current valuation model input layout version.
Ask the Policy Admin Ops Lead in writing whether any release, conversion or block migration landed in the quarter that changes product codes, status codes or key dates.
Record the specification version, cut-off timestamp and any release notes on the quarter's reconciliation cover sheet.
checklist.done: the cover sheet names the valuation date, cut-off timestamp, specification version and every in-quarter admin release affecting the extract.

checklist.step: Pull the seriatim in-force extract from the policy administration system
actions: Run the scheduled quarter-end seriatim job against the frozen cut-off timestamp, one file per writing entity and product family.
Capture the run log: row count, sum of face amount, sum of account value, sum of annualised premium and the file hash for each entity.
Publish the files to the valuation landing zone in the enterprise data warehouse with the naming pattern entity-product-YYYYQn-vN.
Send the run-log summary to the Valuation Actuary and Data Quality Analyst the same day, and never re-run the job without incrementing the version suffix.
checklist.done: versioned extract files are in the valuation landing zone with a run log carrying row counts, control sums and hashes per entity.

checklist.step: Reconcile record counts by product, entity and policy status
actions: Run the policy-count query on the extract grouped by entity, product code and status (in force, paid-up, disabled/waiver, lapsed-in-quarter, death-pending).
Pull the matching counts straight from the policy administration reporting views for the same cut-off and put them side by side.
Roll counts forward from prior quarter: opening + issues + reinstatements - deaths - surrenders - lapses - maturities = closing, and prove the identity holds per product.
List every product where the identity fails with the signed difference and pass it to the Reserving Analyst.
checklist.done: the count roll-forward identity holds by entity and product, or each failure is listed with its signed difference and owner.

checklist.step: Tie extract control totals to the policy administration control report
actions: Sum face amount, account value, cash surrender value and annualised premium from the extract by entity and product.
Open the policy administration quarter-end control report and compare each control sum line by line.
Express each difference in absolute currency and as a percentage of the admin figure and test it against the tolerance table.
Investigate any product where a count matches but an amount does not — that pattern points at a currency, factor or units mapping defect.
Record the tie-out grid, tolerances and pass/fail flags on the reconciliation workbook 'Control Totals' tab.
checklist.done: every control total is compared to the admin control report with a signed difference, a tolerance test and a pass/fail flag.

checklist.step: Reconcile premium and deposit cash to the general ledger
actions: Extract the quarter's premium, deposit and withdrawal postings by entity and product from the general ledger.
Compare them to the same measures summed from the seriatim extract transaction fields.
Split any difference into timing (cash received after the cut-off), suspense/unapplied cash, and genuine data defects, and quantify each bucket.
Hand suspense balances to the Cash Application Specialist with the policy numbers attached and a clearing date.
Sign the cash tie-out sheet and attach the ledger extract behind it.
checklist.done: the premium and deposit difference to the ledger is fully explained across timing, suspense and defect buckets with owners named.

checklist.step: Run the field-level data quality gate on the extract
actions: Execute the valuation data-quality rule pack: null checks on issue date, birth date, sex, plan code, rate class, mode and face amount; range checks on issue age 0-99 and interest rate 0-15%; referential checks on plan code against the product master.
Test business logic: issue date not after the valuation date, maturity date after issue date, account value non-negative, paid-to-date within 13 months of the valuation date.
Produce the failure register with rule id, failing policy count, sample policy numbers and the estimated reserve exposure of each rule.
Block the load where any severity-1 rule fails and notify the Valuation Actuary immediately rather than defaulting the field.
checklist.done: the rule pack has run, the failure register is produced with reserve exposure per rule, and no severity-1 failure is left open at load time.

checklist.step: Reconcile reinsurance ceded flags and treaty codes on the extract
actions: Extract ceded policy keys, treaty codes, quota shares and retention amounts from the reinsurance administration system for the same cut-off.
Join to the seriatim extract on policy number and compare the ceded flag, treaty code and ceded amount at risk policy by policy.
List policies flagged ceded on one side only, and policies whose ceded amount differs by more than 1% of net amount at risk.
Send the break list to the Reinsurance Ops Manager for correction and record the expected fix release.
Quantify the gross-to-net reserve impact of the open breaks for the Valuation Actuary.
checklist.done: ceded flags, treaty codes and ceded amounts agree policy by policy, or each break is listed with its gross-to-net reserve impact.

checklist.step: Load the accepted file into the valuation model and prove the load
actions: Load the versioned extract into the quarter's valuation run and open the model load/validation report.
Compare model-point count and summed face amount, account value and annual premium in the load report to the extract control totals proven earlier — they must be identical, not merely close.
Read the model's rejected-record and defaulted-field listing and quantify the reserve carried by every rejected model point.
Reject the load and go back to the extract where any record is silently dropped or a rate class is defaulted.
Attach the load report and the model run id to the reconciliation workbook.
checklist.done: model point counts and control sums equal the extract exactly, and every rejected or defaulted record is listed with its reserve exposure.

checklist.step: Reconcile modelled reserves to the prior-quarter roll-forward
actions: Build the reserve roll-forward by product: opening reserve + new business + expected accretion of interest - benefits paid - surrenders - maturities +/- assumption change +/- data change = closing reserve.
Run the model on prior-quarter data with current-quarter assumptions to isolate the assumption effect from the data effect.
Attribute any residual movement to a named driver and quantify it; leave nothing in an unexplained bucket above 0.05% of product reserves.
Where the data-change bucket is material, trace it back to the specific break rows in the break log.
checklist.done: the closing reserve is explained by named roll-forward drivers with the unexplained residual inside 0.05% of product reserves.

checklist.step: Classify, quantify and prioritise every break
actions: Give each break a classification code: SOURCE (admin data defect), EXTRACT (job or mapping defect), TIMING (post-cut-off activity), MODEL (load or mapping defect) or ACCEPTED (immaterial, within tolerance).
Quantify each break in policy count and in reserve currency, gross and net of reinsurance.
Rank breaks by reserve impact and mark every break over the tolerance as blocking for the quarter's sign-off.
Assign a named owner and a target fix release to each SOURCE and EXTRACT break.
checklist.done: every break carries a classification code, a policy and reserve quantification, an owner and a target fix release.

checklist.step: Drive source-system corrections with policy administration
actions: Take the SOURCE break list and open a correction ticket per defect with the affected policy numbers attached.
Correct the records in the administration system with a maker-checker pair and record the correction date on each ticket.
Tell the Valuation Actuary in writing which corrections land before the current quarter's cut-off and which slip to next quarter.
Feed defects that recur in two consecutive quarters into the data governance backlog as a control fix, not another manual correction.
checklist.done: every SOURCE break has a correction ticket with a maker-checker record and a stated landing quarter.

checklist.step: Apply, cap and document any valuation data override
actions: Write each override on the override schedule: policy set, field overridden, value used, basis for the value, and the reserve effect gross and net.
Cap the total override effect at the entity materiality set by the Appointed Actuary and stop the load where the cap is breached.
Apply overrides through a versioned, re-runnable script in the staging layer — never by editing the model input file by hand.
Route the override schedule to the Appointed Actuary for signature before the reserve run is declared final.
checklist.done: every override is on the schedule with a basis and reserve effect, sits inside the materiality cap, and is applied by versioned script.

checklist.step: Reconcile the booked reserve back to the general ledger
actions: Take the final reserve summary by entity, product and ledger account from the valuation run.
Compare it to the posted reserve balances in the general ledger after the reserve journal is booked.
Investigate any account-level difference and confirm the journal reference, entity and currency translation rate used.
Sign the reserve-to-ledger tie-out and file it with the close binder for the quarter.
checklist.done: posted reserve balances equal the valuation run by entity, product and account, with the tie-out signed.

checklist.step: Produce and sign the quarterly reconciliation report
actions: Assemble the report: valuation date, extract versions and hashes, count and control-total tie-outs, data-quality failure register, break log with classification and reserve impact, override schedule and ledger tie-out.
State a conclusion on the completeness and accuracy of the valuation data for the quarter and name the residual limitations.
Sign and date the report and reference it from the actuarial reserve memorandum supporting the entity's statutory and group filings.
Report unresolved breaks above tolerance to the Chief Risk Officer and the Audit Committee at the next sitting.
checklist.done: a signed, dated reconciliation report with a stated data conclusion is referenced in the quarter's actuarial memorandum.

checklist.step: File the evidence and feed the data governance backlog
actions: Move the reconciliation workbook, run logs, failure register, break log, override schedule and signed report into the compliance evidence repository under Valuation / ICP 14 / the valuation quarter.
Apply the 10-year-from-valuation-date retention label so the record survives block sale or system decommission.
Open or update a data-quality backlog item for every recurring break with the defect rate trend across the last four quarters.
Confirm the record is indexed and retrievable by entity, valuation date and break classification.
checklist.done: the quarter's reconciliation pack is filed under a 10-year retention label and every recurring break has a backlog item with a trend.

testing.step: Build the population of quarterly reconciliations and the reserves booked from them
actions: List every valuation entity and product line required to reconcile, and every quarter in the test year, to give the expected reconciliation count.
Pull the reconciliation packs actually filed in the evidence repository and the booked reserve balances by entity, product and quarter from the ledger.
Identify entities or quarters with no pack filed and treat each as an automatic exception before any sampling begins.
testing.done: the expected reconciliation population is enumerated and every missing pack is already logged as an exception.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the close calendar and the filed statements
actions: Tie the reserve totals in each pack to the reserve figures in the entity's filed statutory or QRT return for the same date.
Confirm each pack's sign-off date falls on or before the close calendar's WD 10 actuarial sign-off milestone.
List any pack signed after the reserves were booked or after the return was filed as a control-sequencing exception.
testing.done: every pack's reserve total agrees to the filed return and its sign-off date pre-dates the booking, or the difference is listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of entity-quarters where the break log shows a reserve impact above the entity tolerance.
Add 20 entity-product-quarter cells drawn at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population, minimum 30 cells in total.
Record population size, seed, draw date and selection tool in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn that includes every above-tolerance break entity-quarter.

testing.step: Re-extract the seriatim data independently and compare to the pack
actions: Re-run the seriatim query against the frozen quarter-end snapshot for each sampled entity-product without using the team's saved file.
Compare row count, face amount, account value and annualised premium to the control totals in the pack and to the file hash recorded in the run log.
Where hashes differ, establish whether the job was re-run after sign-off and whether the reconciliation was redone against the later version.
Capture the independent query, its parameters and its output into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled extract reproduces the pack's control totals and hash, or the divergence is documented with its cause.

testing.step: Re-perform the count roll-forward and the control-total tie-out
actions: Recompute opening + issues + reinstatements - deaths - surrenders - lapses - maturities = closing for each sampled product without reference to the team's workbook.
Recompute each control-total difference and its percentage against the admin control report figure.
Compare your own numbers to the pack cell by cell and treat any difference, including a right answer supported by the wrong figure, as an exception.
Note any tolerance that was applied at a level higher than the one written in the approved tolerance table.
testing.done: the roll-forward and control totals are independently reproduced for every sampled cell with differences listed.

testing.step: Trace sampled breaks to root cause and to evidence of the fix
actions: Pick 15 breaks from the sampled packs, weighted to the largest reserve impacts, and open each one's data-quality issue record.
Confirm the classification code matches the evidence, the affected policy list is attached and the reserve impact is quantified gross and net.
Follow each SOURCE break to the correction ticket in the administration system and confirm the maker-checker record and correction date.
Check the following quarter's pack to confirm the break did not recur; a recurrence with no control change is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled break traces to a classified issue, a quantified impact and evidence the correction was made and held.

testing.step: Recompute the tolerance and materiality maths
actions: Recompute the entity tolerance as 0.05% of gross policy reserves and compare it to the USD 250k absolute floor to see which binds.
Recompute each sampled quarter's aggregate unexplained difference and test it against the binding tolerance.
Recompute the total override effect and test it against the materiality cap set by the Appointed Actuary.
Flag any quarter signed off where the recomputed figure breaches a threshold the pack reported as passing.
testing.done: tolerances, aggregate differences and the override cap are independently recomputed and every threshold breach is flagged.

testing.step: Test override authorisation and sign-off sequencing
actions: Pull the override schedule for every sampled quarter and confirm each override names the field, the value used and the basis for it.
Confirm the Appointed Actuary's signature carries a date on or before the reserve run declared final and before the ledger posting date.
Confirm each override was applied by a versioned script in staging and re-run to the same result, not by a manual file edit.
Treat any override applied without a pre-dated signature as a control failure rather than a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled override is authorised, dated ahead of booking and reproducible from a versioned script.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying entity, quarter, product, the control that failed and the reserve exposed.
Assign a root cause from the standing list (extract specification drift, admin release untested, tolerance misapplied, unauthorised override, late sign-off) and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next close cycle and require a control change, not a manual workaround, for anything recurring.
Carry every open issue into the next test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue record with a root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate over sampled cells and compare it to the zero-count-difference and 0.05% reserve thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared none of the sampled reconciliations, sign the workpaper with a date.
Report the conclusion and any unresolved reserve exposure to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states an exception rate, a conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date, and is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns every substantive response to a supervisor's valuation inquiry, including group-wide supervisor and college questions on reserves, assumptions and asset adequacy

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 14 (Valuation) and ICP 9 (Supervisory Review and Reporting) Standards 9.1-9.4 on responding to supervisory requests, with ICP 25 / ComFrame on group-wide supervision and college information sharing; each inquiry is answered against the citing supervisor's own local rule (VM-30/VM-31, Solvency II Art. 35, OSFI E-15) checked at intake

In-scope processes.value: Intake, clocking, drafting, review and submission of every written valuation inquiry from a local supervisor, the group-wide supervisor or a supervisory college, plus the follow-up cycle until the file is closed

In-scope systems.value: Inquiry register holds the request, deadline clock, drafts, approvals and the submitted package; regulator portals (NAIC iSite+, PRA RegData, OSFI RRS, EIOPA national portals) carry the actual submission

Compliance procedure documented.value: Valuation Inquiry Response Procedure — intake and logging within 1 business day, scoping call, evidence pull from the valuation run, drafting, actuarial and legal review, submission and closure

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the Head of Compliance; reviewed annually and after any inquiry that missed its deadline

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Deadline is whatever the inquiry letter states, commonly 10 to 30 calendar days; the register stores the letter date, receipt date, stated due date and the internal draft-ready date set at due date minus 5 business days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Register alerts fire to the Appointed Actuary and Regulatory Affairs Manager at receipt, at due date minus 10, minus 5 and minus 2 business days, and daily once overdue

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Inquiry letter, scoping notes, model run ids and exhibits relied on, all drafts, reviewer sign-offs and the submission receipt retained 10 years from closure in the correspondence file

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any inquiry answered after its stated due date, or any answer later corrected, is logged with the days late, the cause and the corrective action

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs every late response, every supplementary correction to a prior answer and any change to reserves triggered by the inquiry

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All valuation inquiries received in the period across every supervised entity, taken from the inquiry register plus an independent sweep of the regulatory mailbox and portal message centres

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missed statutory due dates and on unlogged inquiries; any answer whose figures cannot be reproduced from the cited model run id is a fail; two or more late responses in a period escalates to the Audit Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; testing runs semi-annually over every inquiry received in the half, with 100% coverage of inquiries that changed a reserve or an assumption

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Must not have drafted, reviewed or submitted any sampled response and must sit outside the actuarial function

Evidence location for test results.value: Valuation inquiry response test workpaper (register extract, mailbox sweep, sample, re-performance of cited figures, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Supervisory Correspondence

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A complete correspondence file per inquiry — letter, response, exhibits, model run ids, sign-offs and submission receipt — retrievable within 3 business days for a follow-up question or an on-site inspection

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager is the single channel to the supervisor; Appointed Actuary owns the technical content; Regulatory Counsel clears anything conceding an error, a restatement or a control weakness before it is sent

checklist.step: Intake the inquiry and open a numbered correspondence file
actions: Sweep the regulatory mailbox and the portal message centres (NAIC iSite+ messages, PRA RegData notices, OSFI RRS correspondence) each business day for new inquiries.
Create a register entry within one business day carrying supervisor name, entity, letter date, receipt date, stated due date, subject and the reserve or assumption area named.
Attach the inquiry letter and any regulator attachments, and assign the file number in the pattern INQ-<entity>-<year>-<seq>.
Notify the Appointed Actuary, Chief Actuary and Regulatory Counsel the same day with the due date in the subject line.
checklist.done: the inquiry is registered inside one business day with letter date, due date and named owners, and the letter is attached.

checklist.step: Clock the deadline and set the internal milestones
actions: Read the letter for the response period stated (commonly 10, 20 or 30 calendar days) and whether it runs from the letter date or the receipt date.
Compute the internal draft-ready date as the due date minus 5 business days and the review-complete date as the due date minus 2 business days.
Load the due date and both milestones into the register and switch on the minus-10, minus-5 and minus-2 business-day alerts.
Where the period is genuinely unworkable, request an extension in writing from the supervisor before the halfway point and record the reply on the file.
checklist.done: the register carries the stated due date, both internal milestones and live alerts, with any extension request evidenced in writing.

checklist.step: Scope the question with the supervisor rather than guessing
actions: Break the letter into numbered sub-questions and mark each as data, methodology, assumption, governance or opinion.
Identify the exact valuation date, entity, product line and basis (statutory, GAAP, Solvency II, IFRS 17) each sub-question refers to.
Where a sub-question is ambiguous, ask the named supervisory contact a written clarifying question through the Regulatory Affairs Manager and record the answer on the file.
Publish the numbered sub-question list as the response skeleton so nothing is answered twice or missed.
checklist.done: a numbered sub-question list exists with basis, entity and valuation date fixed for each, and any ambiguity resolved in writing.

checklist.step: Pull the source evidence from the cited valuation run
actions: Identify the model run id, assumption set version and in-force file version behind the figures the supervisor is asking about.
Re-open that archived run and export the exhibits needed — reserve by product, roll-forward, sensitivity and asset adequacy cash flow testing output.
Tie every exported figure back to the figure as filed in the statutory return or QRT so the response cannot contradict the filing.
Where the filed figure cannot be reproduced, stop and escalate to the Chief Actuary before drafting anything.
checklist.done: each sub-question has exhibits exported from a named archived run that reproduce the filed figures exactly.

checklist.step: Reconstruct the assumption basis and its governance trail
actions: For each assumption questioned (mortality, lapse, expense, discount rate, morbidity), retrieve the experience study that set it, its date and its credibility conclusion.
Retrieve the assumption approval record — committee, date, minute reference — and the margin or provision for adverse deviation applied.
Explain any change since the prior valuation with the driver, the effective quarter and the reserve impact of the change.
Assemble these into an assumption annex the response can cite by paragraph number.
checklist.done: every questioned assumption has an experience study, a dated approval reference and a quantified change explanation in the annex.

checklist.step: Draft the response answering each sub-question in its own numbered section
actions: Mirror the supervisor's numbering exactly so section 3(b) of the reply answers question 3(b) of the letter.
Give the direct answer first, then the basis, then the exhibit reference; never answer a valuation question with a process description alone.
State the local requirement being satisfied for each answer (for example VM-31 Section 3 for the PBR report, Solvency II Art. 82 for data quality) alongside the ICP the supervisor cited.
Mark clearly where an answer is an estimate, what it is sensitive to, and what would change it.
Attach the exhibits as lettered appendices and list them in a schedule at the front.
checklist.done: a numbered draft answers every sub-question with a direct answer, a stated basis and a lettered exhibit reference.

checklist.step: Run the technical review against the exhibits
actions: Take the draft and independently trace every number in the text back to the appendix exhibit and the model run id.
Recompute at least the reserve totals, the roll-forward drivers and any percentage or ratio quoted in the narrative.
Challenge any statement that goes beyond what the exhibits actually show and require it to be cut or evidenced.
Record the review on the file with the reviewer name, date and the list of changes required.
checklist.done: every figure in the draft is traced and recomputed by a second actuary, with the review and required changes recorded.

checklist.step: Run the legal and privilege review
actions: Read the draft for any admission of error, control weakness, breach or prospective restatement and confirm the wording is accurate and intended.
Confirm no privileged legal advice, unrelated litigation material or third-party confidential data is carried in the exhibits.
Confirm the response does not contradict statements made to another supervisor on the same subject in the last 24 months by checking the register.
Give a written clearance on the file, or return the draft with specific wording changes.
checklist.done: counsel has cleared the draft in writing or returned specific wording changes, with no unintended admission or privileged content left in.

checklist.step: Obtain the final approval and signature
actions: Review the cleared draft against the original letter to confirm every sub-question is answered and nothing was dropped in review.
Confirm the exhibit schedule matches the attachments actually present and that each attachment is legible and text-searchable.
Sign the response in the capacity the supervisor asked for — Appointed Actuary signature where an actuarial opinion is being given.
Record the signature name, capacity and date on the register entry.
checklist.done: the final response is signed in the requested capacity with a complete, legible exhibit set and the signature logged.

checklist.step: Submit through the channel the supervisor specified and capture the receipt
actions: Use the channel named in the letter — the portal message centre (NAIC iSite+, PRA RegData, OSFI RRS, APRA Connect), the named examiner's secure email, or the supervisory college secretariat.
Check attachment size and format limits before uploading and split large exhibit sets rather than letting an upload fail near the deadline.
Capture the confirmation number, the timestamp and a screenshot of the submitted state into the correspondence file.
Update the register status to Submitted with the actual submission date and compute days early or late against the due date.
checklist.done: the response is submitted through the specified channel with a captured confirmation and the register showing the actual submission date.

checklist.step: Work the follow-up cycle until the supervisor closes the point
actions: Log every follow-up question, call or meeting on the same file number with its own due date rather than opening a new file.
Prepare a written note before any supervisory call listing the points to be made and the figures that support them, and circulate a minute afterwards the same day.
Answer follow-ups against the same exhibits, and reissue an exhibit with a new version number where a figure has moved.
Ask the supervisor in writing to confirm closure where the file has been quiet for 30 days.
checklist.done: every follow-up sits on the original file with its own due date, and closure is either confirmed by the supervisor or actively chased.

checklist.step: Convert supervisory findings into actual remediation
actions: Extract every recommendation, expectation or criticism from the supervisor's follow-up correspondence into a numbered finding list.
Raise a GRC issue per finding with an owner, an agreed action, a due date and the evidence that will close it.
Report the finding list and its status to the Risk Committee at its next sitting and monthly thereafter until closed.
Confirm back to the supervisor in writing when each action is complete, attaching the closing evidence.
checklist.done: each supervisory finding is a tracked issue with an owner, a due date and a written completion confirmation to the supervisor.

checklist.step: Feed the answer back into the valuation process so the same question is not asked twice
actions: Where the inquiry exposed a documentation gap, add the missing explanation to the standing actuarial report section for the next valuation.
Where it exposed a methodology weakness, put the change on the assumption or methodology agenda with an owner and a target valuation date.
Where it exposed a data defect, open a data-quality issue linked to the reserve reconciliation break log.
Record on the register which process change each inquiry produced, or state explicitly that none was needed and why.
checklist.done: the register records a named process change per inquiry, or a reasoned statement that none was required.

checklist.step: Report inquiry activity to the board committee
actions: Prepare a quarterly schedule of open and closed valuation inquiries by supervisor, subject, due date, submission date and days late.
Highlight any inquiry that changed a reserve, an assumption or a filed figure, with the amount.
Table the schedule at the Audit Committee and record the minute reference on each affected register entry.
Escalate immediately, outside the quarterly cycle, any inquiry alleging a breach or requesting a restatement.
checklist.done: the committee has a dated schedule of inquiries with minute references recorded back on the register entries.

checklist.step: Close and retain the correspondence file
actions: Confirm the file holds the letter, sub-question list, exhibits with run ids, all drafts, technical and legal reviews, the signed response and the submission receipt.
Set the register status to Closed with the closure date and the basis for closure (supervisor confirmation or 30-day quiet period).
Move the file to the compliance evidence repository under Supervisory Correspondence and apply the 10-year-from-closure retention label.
Confirm it is indexed and retrievable by supervisor, entity, valuation date and subject.
checklist.done: a complete file is closed, filed under a 10-year retention label and retrievable by supervisor, entity and subject.

testing.step: Build the population of inquiries actually received
actions: Export every inquiry register entry for the period with supervisor, entity, letter date, receipt date, due date, submission date and status.
Sweep independently: the regulatory mailbox, the portal message centres for each supervised entity, and the Appointed Actuary's inbox for supervisor domains, over the same period.
List inquiries found in the sweep but absent from the register — each is an automatic exception regardless of whether it was answered.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the register population is reconciled to an independent mailbox and portal sweep, with unlogged inquiries already exceptions.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the supervisors' own records
actions: For each supervised entity, open the portal correspondence history and list the inbound and outbound items the supervisor holds for the period.
Match each portal item to a register file number and to a submitted response.
Investigate any outbound submission with no register entry — an answer sent outside the process is a control failure.
Record the reconciliation, including counts inbound and outbound per supervisor, in the workpaper.
testing.done: portal correspondence history reconciles item for item to the register, with unmatched items investigated and written up.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of inquiries that changed a reserve, an assumption or a filed figure, and 100% of inquiries submitted after their due date.
Add 12 inquiries drawn at random with a recorded seed from the remainder, minimum 20 files in total.
Record the population size, the seed, the draw date and the selection tool in the workpaper.
Where the population is smaller than 20, test it in full and say so.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers every reserve-changing and every late inquiry plus a seeded random remainder.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths on every sampled file
actions: Read the response period from the letter itself, not the register, and note whether it runs from the letter date or the receipt date.
Recompute the due date and compare it to the register value; a wrongly clocked deadline is an exception even where the answer was timely.
Compute days early or late as submission date minus due date and compare to the register's own figure.
Confirm any extension claimed is evidenced by a written supervisor reply on the file, dated before the original due date.
testing.done: due dates and days-late are recomputed from the letters, with every clocking difference and unevidenced extension listed.

testing.step: Re-perform the cited figures from the archived model run
actions: For each sampled response, take the model run id and assumption set version cited and re-open the archived run.
Reproduce at least three quantitative statements from the response text directly from the run output.
Tie those same figures to the entity's filed statutory return or QRT for the valuation date concerned.
Treat any figure that cannot be reproduced, or that contradicts the filing, as a fail rather than a presentational point.
testing.done: at least three figures per sampled response are reproduced from the cited run and tie to the filed return.

testing.step: Test completeness of the answer against the letter
actions: Read each sampled letter and build your own numbered sub-question list without looking at the response skeleton.
Map each sub-question to the section of the response that answers it and mark any that is unanswered or answered only by process narrative.
Check that the answer addresses the basis, entity and valuation date the supervisor named, not a convenient adjacent one.
List every gap with the letter paragraph reference.
testing.done: every sub-question in each sampled letter is mapped to a substantive answer, or the gap is listed with its paragraph reference.

testing.step: Test the review and approval chain on the sample
actions: Confirm a technical review by a second actuary exists, is dated before submission and lists the changes required.
Confirm counsel clearance exists and pre-dates submission for any response containing an admission, a restatement or a control weakness.
Confirm the signature capacity on the response matches what the letter demanded, particularly where an Appointed Actuary opinion was requested.
Treat a sign-off dated after the submission timestamp as an unapproved submission.
testing.done: each sampled response shows technical review, required legal clearance and a correct signature capacity, all dated before submission.

testing.step: Trace the follow-up and remediation trail to completion
actions: For each sampled file, list the supervisory findings raised in follow-up correspondence and match them to GRC issue records.
Confirm each issue carries an owner, an agreed action, a due date and closing evidence, and check the closing evidence actually demonstrates the action.
Confirm the written completion confirmation to the supervisor exists and post-dates the closing evidence.
Flag findings closed on assertion alone with no attached evidence.
testing.done: each supervisory finding traces to a tracked issue with real closing evidence and a dated confirmation to the supervisor.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the file number, supervisor, entity, the control that failed and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the standing list (inquiry never registered, deadline miscalculated, figure not reproducible, review skipped, submitted outside the channel) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missed statutory due date, require a written process change signed by the Chief Actuary.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with a root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time response rate and the unlogged-inquiry count and compare both to the zero-tolerance thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted or reviewed none of the sampled responses, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, the late-response count and any unresolved supervisory finding to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time rate, a conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date, and is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Fix and publish the in-scope definition
actions: Write the in-scope test: any model, rule set, score or algorithm whose output influences a pricing, underwriting, claims, fraud, servicing or marketing decision about a customer or prospect, whether built in-house, bought, or embedded in a platform.

State explicitly that deterministic rating algorithms, vendor scores consumed through an API, and business rules configured in the policy or claims platform are in scope, and that pure infrastructure and reporting models are not.
Take the definition through the AI Governance Committee and record the approving minute reference.
Publish the definition to every model owner and to procurement so new vendor tools are caught at contract stage.
checklist.done: a committee-approved in-scope definition is published with worked inclusions and exclusions and a minute reference.

checklist.step: Sweep the technical registries for candidate models
actions: Export every registered model from the MLflow/Azure ML registry with name, version, stage (staging, production, archived), owner and last deployment date.
Export served endpoints from the serving layer and match them to registry entries so a deployed-but-unregistered artefact stands out.
Export notebooks and jobs from the Databricks workspace that write to a scoring table, and list the ones running on a schedule.
Deliver the combined candidate list to the AI Governance Analyst with a run date and the query used.
checklist.done: a dated candidate list from the model registry, serving endpoints and scheduled scoring jobs is delivered with its queries.

checklist.step: Sweep the business platforms for embedded models and rule sets
actions: List the rating algorithms, rating tables and underwriting rule sets configured in the policy administration and rating platforms per product and jurisdiction.
List the claims platform rules that route, segment, triage or auto-adjudicate, including straight-through-processing thresholds.
List the pricing and optimisation models configured in the rating engine, including demand and elasticity models.
Mark which of these consume an external score and record the calling interface for each.
checklist.done: every rating, underwriting and claims rule set or model configured in the business platforms is listed with its product and jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Sweep procurement and vendor contracts for bought-in models
actions: Search the vendor master and contract repository for suppliers of scores, models, analytics or decisioning services.
For each, record the vendor, the product name, the decisions it feeds, the contract owner and the renewal date.
Request from every such vendor the model documentation, the data the model is trained on and the vendor's own testing and governance evidence, citing the contractual audit clause.
Flag vendors that decline to supply documentation for escalation to the AI Governance Committee, since undocumented vendor models cannot be governed.
checklist.done: every contracted model or score supplier is listed with its decisions, contract owner and documentation status.

checklist.step: Sweep the analytics estate for end-user-computing models
actions: Query the warehouse for tables and views whose names or column patterns indicate scores, propensities, tiers, segments or predictions, and list their producing jobs.
Interview each business area's analytics lead for spreadsheets or desktop tools that produce a score used in a live decision.
Record each finding with the producer, the consuming decision, the refresh cadence and whether any human reviews the output before it acts.
Route material end-user-computing models to the model registration gate rather than leaving them in spreadsheets.
checklist.done: spreadsheet and warehouse-resident scoring models are identified with their consuming decision and refresh cadence.

checklist.step: Deduplicate the candidate list into distinct model records
actions: Merge candidates that are the same logical model surfaced through different artefacts, keeping versions under one parent model id.
Split candidates that share code but are separately trained or calibrated per jurisdiction or product into distinct records.
Assign a permanent model id in the pattern MDL-<domain>-<seq> that survives retraining and platform migration.
Record the source sweep that found each record so coverage of each sweep can be measured.
checklist.done: a deduplicated model register exists with permanent ids, correct version parenting and the discovering sweep recorded.

checklist.step: Capture the mandatory attribute set for every model
actions: Complete for each model: business purpose, the decision it influences, in-scope products and jurisdictions, model technique, training data sources and vintage, feature list, target variable, output type and its use threshold.
Record the model owner (accountable business executive), the developer, the validator and the operating team, by name and role.
Record lifecycle status (development, validation, production, monitored, retired), production release date and the date of the last validation and last bias test.
Record whether protected or proxy-sensitive attributes are used, inferred or excluded, and how that was determined.
Leave no mandatory field blank — an unknown value is itself a finding and must be raised as an issue.
checklist.done: every model record carries the full mandatory attribute set with named people and no blank mandatory fields.

checklist.step: Risk-tier each model against the published criteria
actions: Score each model on consumer impact (does it decline, price, restrict or reduce a benefit), autonomy (fully automated versus advisory), population reach and data sensitivity.
Assign tier 1 (high) where the model can adversely affect a consumer without human review, tier 2 where a human reviews before action, tier 3 for internal or advisory use.
Attach the tier-driven control set: tier 1 requires independent validation, annual bias testing, documented human oversight and board-level reporting.
Record any tier override with the reasoning and sign it personally.
checklist.done: every model carries a scored tier, the control set that tier demands, and a signed reason for any override.

checklist.step: Map each model to its jurisdiction footprint and applicable rules
actions: For each model, list the jurisdictions whose policyholders it touches, taken from the products and entities it serves rather than from where it was built.

Attach the local requirements that bite in each: NAIC AI bulletin adoption status by state, Colorado quantitative testing regulation for life underwriting, NY DFS Circular Letter 7 for underwriting and pricing, EU AI Act risk classification, local privacy law for the features used.
Flag models whose footprint includes a jurisdiction with a filing, attestation or testing obligation and set the recurring obligation on the compliance calendar.
Escalate models operating in a jurisdiction whose requirements the current control set does not meet.
checklist.done: every model has a jurisdiction list with the specific local obligations attached and calendar entries for the recurring ones.

checklist.step: Gate production release on registration
actions: Add a pipeline check that reads the model id from the deployment manifest and calls the model governance repository to confirm an active registered record.
Fail the deployment where the id is missing, the record is incomplete, or a tier 1 model has no current validation and bias test.
Require a named break-glass approval from the Model Risk Manager, recorded with an expiry date, for any emergency bypass.
Publish the monthly count of blocked and bypassed deployments to the AI Governance Committee.
checklist.done: no model reaches production without an active registry record, and every bypass is named, dated and expiring.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly owner attestation
actions: Issue each model owner their model records at quarter end plus 5 working days and require confirmation of purpose, status, tier, data sources and human oversight design.
Require owners to declare new models, retrained versions, changed thresholds and models retired during the quarter.
Chase non-responders at plus 10 working days and escalate to the Chief Data Officer at plus 12.
Close the cycle by the 15th working day with a completion percentage reported to the AI Governance Committee.
checklist.done: the quarterly attestation closes by working day 15 with a reported completion rate and every declaration recorded.

checklist.step: Reconcile the inventory to production reality every quarter
actions: Re-run the registry, platform, vendor and warehouse sweeps and compare the results to the current inventory.
Produce two lists: production artefacts with no inventory record (shadow models) and inventory records with no production footprint (stale records).
Investigate each shadow model for what decisions it has already influenced and over what period.
Raise a GRC issue per shadow model and retire stale records with a documented retirement date and archive location.
checklist.done: each quarter's sweep produces a reconciled shadow-model and stale-record list with an issue or retirement per line.

checklist.step: Handle retirement without losing the record
actions: On retirement, capture the final version artefacts, the last validation report, the last bias test and the decisions the model made in its final year.
Set status to Retired with the retirement date, the reason and the replacement model id where one exists.
Apply the 7-year-from-retirement retention label so a supervisor can still be answered about a decommissioned model.
Confirm the retired record remains searchable by jurisdiction and business use.
checklist.done: retired models keep a complete, searchable record under a 7-year-from-retirement retention label.

checklist.step: Report the inventory to the AI Governance Committee and the board
actions: Produce the quarterly inventory dashboard: model counts by tier, business use and jurisdiction; new, retrained and retired in the quarter; overdue validations and bias tests; open shadow-model issues.
Highlight the tier 1 models that can adversely affect a consumer without human review and the controls sitting on each.
Table it at the AI Governance Committee and at least annually at the board risk committee, and record the minute reference.
Certify inventory completeness in writing on the quarterly pack.
checklist.done: a quarterly dashboard with a written completeness certification is tabled and minuted at the governance committee.

checklist.step: Keep the inventory export supervisor-ready
actions: Maintain a standing export template covering model id, business use, decision affected, tier, jurisdictions, data sources, human oversight design, last validation and last bias test date.
Refresh the export each quarter and file the dated snapshot in the compliance evidence repository under AI Governance.
Dry-run the export annually against a real supervisory AI data call format (for example a state AI survey or an EIOPA questionnaire) and time how long it takes to produce.
Fix any field the dry run shows cannot be produced from the inventory as it stands.
checklist.done: a dated, supervisor-format inventory snapshot exists each quarter and the annual dry run produces it inside the target turnaround.

testing.step: Build the population of production models independently of the inventory
actions: Pull production-stage models and live serving endpoints from the model registry and serving layer directly, not from the governance repository.
Add the rating, underwriting and claims rule sets configured in the business platforms and the scores consumed from vendor APIs, taken from interface logs.
Add scheduled warehouse scoring jobs writing to tables consumed by a decisioning process.
Sign the combined list as the test population, recording each query and the date it was run.
testing.done: an independently sourced production-model population is signed as complete with queries and run dates recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the independent population to the inventory of record
actions: Match each population item to a model record on model id, artefact name and endpoint.
List unmatched production items as shadow models and unmatched inventory records as stale entries.
For every shadow model, establish from interface or decision logs how many customer decisions it influenced and over what period.
Quantify the reconciliation as a coverage percentage and treat any shadow model touching a consumer decision as a reportable failure.
testing.done: coverage is quantified and every shadow model is identified with the customer decisions it influenced.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of tier 1 models and 100% of models added or retrained in the period.
Add 15 models drawn at random with a recorded seed from tiers 2 and 3, minimum 25 records in total.
Include at least three vendor-supplied models and three platform-embedded rule sets so the sample is not all in-house code.
Record population size, seed, draw date and stratification in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible, stratified sample covers all tier 1 and new models plus vendor and platform-embedded records.

testing.step: Test attribute completeness and accuracy on the sample
actions: Check every mandatory field is populated on each sampled record and that no field carries a placeholder such as TBD or Unknown.
Verify the feature list against the model's actual scoring code or the vendor's documentation and flag any feature present in code but absent from the record.
Verify the recorded training data sources against the data lineage in the warehouse catalogue.
Confirm the named owner, developer and validator are current employees in those roles and not leavers.
testing.done: each sampled record is complete, its feature list matches the scoring code, and its named people are current.

testing.step: Re-perform the risk-tier judgement independently
actions: For each sampled model, read the business purpose and decision flow and reach your own tier conclusion before looking at the recorded tier.
Test the autonomy claim against the actual system configuration: confirm a referral or review step really exists where tier 2 is claimed.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded tier and treat any under-tiering as an exception with the control gap it created.
Check that every tier override carries a written reason and a signature.
testing.done: each sampled tier is independently re-derived, with under-tiering listed and every override signed.

testing.step: Test the release gate by attempting a controlled deployment
actions: In a non-production pipeline run, submit a deployment manifest with no model id and confirm the registry check fails the build.
Repeat with a valid id but an incomplete record and with a tier 1 id whose bias test is over a year old, confirming both fail.
Pull the period's list of bypassed deployments and confirm each has a named Model Risk Manager approval with an expiry date that was honoured.
Capture the pipeline logs into the workpaper as evidence the control operates rather than merely exists.
testing.done: the release gate is proven to block unregistered, incomplete and stale-tested models, with every bypass evidenced.

testing.step: Test the quarterly attestation for reach and honesty
actions: Recompute the attestation completion rate from the raw task records and compare it to the rate reported to the committee.
For 10 sampled attestations, compare the owner's declaration to what actually changed in the registry that quarter — retrains, threshold changes and retirements.
Flag attestations confirming no change where the registry or deployment history shows a retrain or a threshold move.
Confirm non-responders were escalated on the stated day counts.
testing.done: the reported completion rate is reproduced and every attestation that contradicts deployment history is flagged.

testing.step: Recompute the currency of validations and bias tests
actions: For each sampled model, compute days since the last validation and days since the last bias test from the recorded dates.
Compare to the tier-driven requirement — annual for tier 1 — and to the 90-day attestation staleness threshold.
Trace each recorded date to the underlying report and confirm the report actually covers the version now in production.
Treat a current date pointing at a report on a superseded model version as a fail.
testing.done: validation and bias-test currency is recomputed per model and each date is traced to a report covering the live version.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying model id, business use, jurisdiction footprint and the consumer decisions exposed.
Assign a root cause from the standing list (discovery sweep missed the source, gate bypassed, attestation inaccurate, tier understated, vendor documentation refused) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; for shadow models touching consumer decisions, require either registration with full documentation or shutdown within 30 days.
Carry every open issue into the next quarterly reconciliation as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute inventory coverage, the shadow-model count and the tier 1 attribute completeness rate against the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references supporting it.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns and attests none of the sampled models, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and every open shadow model to the AI Governance Committee and the board risk committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states coverage, shadow-model count, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, and is filed.
