checklist.step: Select the models due for testing and open a test specification
actions: Filter the inventory for tier 1 and tier 2 models whose last bias test is over 11 months old or whose production version has changed since the last test.
Open a test specification per model recording model id, production version, the decision tested (quote, accept, decline, rate tier, claim referral) and the test window.
Confirm with the model owner which jurisdictions the results must satisfy so the metric set covers the strictest of them.
Book the test into the quarter's plan with a named analyst and a completion date ahead of the 12-month anniversary.
checklist.done: each due model has a dated specification naming version, decision tested, jurisdictions and an owning analyst.

checklist.step: Assemble the scored decision dataset for the test window
actions: Extract every decision the model scored in the window with applicant identifiers, model inputs, model score, the threshold applied and the final decision recorded downstream.
Include declines, referrals and non-take-ups, not just bound business, so adverse outcomes are not filtered out of the population.
Join the downstream outcome from the policy or claims platform to confirm what actually happened to each decision.
Snapshot the dataset with a version id and record the row count, window and query in the specification.
checklist.done: a versioned dataset snapshot holds every scored decision in the window including declines and referrals, with counts recorded.

checklist.step: Derive protected-class indicators using the approved proxy methodology
actions: Where race or ethnicity is not collected, apply Bayesian Improved First Name Surname Geocoding using the Census surname list, the first-name list and the applicant's census block group to produce probability vectors per group.
Use directly collected attributes where they exist and are lawfully usable — sex and age are usually on the application record.
Record the proxy version, the reference data vintage and the geocoding match rate, and exclude records whose geocode failed rather than defaulting them.
Store the proxy assignment in a separate access-controlled table and never write it back to the operational record.
checklist.done: probability-weighted group indicators exist for the population with a recorded match rate and access-controlled storage.

checklist.step: Fix the metric set and thresholds before looking at any result
actions: Write into the specification the metrics to be computed: disparate impact ratio on the favourable outcome, approval-rate gap in percentage points, standardized mean difference of the score, adverse impact ratio at the operating threshold, and calibration by group.
Record the thresholds that will trigger investigation: DI ratio outside 0.80 to 1.25, SMD above 0.20, approval-rate gap above 5 points.
Set the minimum group size for a reportable result at 100 decisions and state what happens below it.
Have the Model Risk Manager sign the specification before the analysis runs so thresholds cannot move after seeing the numbers.
checklist.done: a signed specification fixes metrics, thresholds and minimum group sizes before any result is computed.

checklist.step: Compute the unconditional outcome metrics by group
actions: Compute favourable-outcome rates by group using the probability weights and produce disparate impact ratios against the highest-rate group.
Compute mean and distribution of the model score by group and the standardized mean difference between each group and the reference.
Compute confidence intervals on every ratio and gap so a small-sample swing is not read as a finding.
Produce the results table by jurisdiction and by product as well as in aggregate, since a group-level pass can hide a state-level failure.
checklist.done: outcome rates, ratios, score differences and confidence intervals are computed by group, jurisdiction and product.

checklist.step: Run the conditional analysis on legitimate rating factors
actions: Fit the outcome against the model score with the legitimate, filed rating and underwriting variables entered as controls.
Report the residual group effect after controls with its coefficient, standard error and significance, so it is clear how much disparity the legitimate factors explain.
State explicitly which control variables were used and why each is legitimate, citing the filed rating plan or underwriting guideline.
Flag any control variable that is itself a close proxy for a protected class as unusable and rerun without it.
checklist.done: residual group effects after legitimate controls are reported with significance, and every control is justified by a filed plan or guideline.

checklist.step: Attribute disparity to specific features
actions: Compute per-feature contribution to the score gap between groups using SHAP or an equivalent decomposition on the snapshot dataset.
Rank features by their contribution to the disparity and identify any feature acting as a proxy for a protected class.
Test proxy suspicion directly by regressing the suspect feature on the group indicator and reporting the strength of association.
Write the top contributing features and their association strengths into the test report so remediation has somewhere to start.
checklist.done: the score gap is decomposed to named features with proxy strength measured for each suspect feature.

checklist.step: Test the operating threshold, not just the score
actions: Compute selection rates by group at the threshold actually in production, since a fair score can still be applied at an unfair cut-off.
Recompute the adverse impact ratio across a range of candidate thresholds and plot where the ratio crosses 0.80.
Compute error rates by group at the production threshold — false decline and false accept — and report equalized-odds gaps.
Hand the threshold sensitivity to the model owner as the first remediation lever.
checklist.done: selection and error rates are computed at the production threshold and across candidate thresholds with the fair range identified.

checklist.step: Test the vendor-supplied components inside the model
actions: List every external score or vendor feature feeding the model and request the vendor's own bias testing evidence under the contract's audit clause.
Where the vendor will not disclose, test the vendor score as a black box on the internal population using the same metric set.
Record the vendor's response and the residual uncertainty in the test report rather than treating an untested vendor score as neutral.
Escalate to the AI Governance Committee any vendor input that materially drives disparity and cannot be explained.
checklist.done: every vendor input is either supported by vendor testing evidence or tested as a black box, with the outcome in the report.

checklist.step: Write the bias test report with a stated conclusion
actions: Assemble the report: model id and version, decision tested, window, population and group sizes, proxy methodology and match rate, metric results with confidence intervals, conditional analysis, feature attribution, threshold analysis and vendor position.
State a conclusion per jurisdiction: no evidence of unfair discrimination, indication requiring remediation, or inconclusive with the reason.
Attach the reproducible notebook and the dataset snapshot id so any result can be re-run exactly.
Publish to the model governance repository against the model version tested.
checklist.done: a published report ties every result to a reproducible notebook and states a per-jurisdiction conclusion.

checklist.step: Decide remediation where a threshold is breached
actions: Convene the model owner, Pricing Actuary and Regulatory Counsel within 10 business days of a breached threshold.
Evaluate the options in order: remove or replace the driving feature, retrain with a fairness constraint, move the operating threshold, add human review before adverse action, or withdraw the model.
Quantify the expected effect of the chosen option on both the disparity metric and the business outcome, and record both.
Set an implementation date and a retest date, and record the decision and its rationale in the model record.
checklist.done: each breach has a dated remediation decision with quantified expected effect, an implementation date and a retest date.

checklist.step: Escalate any decision to keep running a breaching model
actions: Require a written case for any model kept in production with an unresolved breach, naming the affected group, the metric, the population size and the consumer impact.
Require the compensating controls to be specific — mandatory human review of adverse decisions in the affected segment, a tightened referral rule, or a capped adverse action rate.
Sign or refuse the case personally and set a hard retest date no more than 90 days out.
Report every such case to the AI Governance Committee and to the board risk committee at its next sitting.
checklist.done: no breaching model runs on without a personally signed case, specific compensating controls and a 90-day retest date.

checklist.step: Retest after remediation and prove the fix
actions: Re-run the full metric set on decisions produced after the remediation went live, using the same specification and proxy version.
Compare pre and post metrics side by side and state whether the disparity actually moved, with confidence intervals.
Confirm the remediation did not simply shift the disparity to another group or another jurisdiction.
Close the GRC issue only on the retest result, never on implementation of the change alone.
checklist.done: a post-remediation retest on live decisions shows the metric movement and the issue is closed on results, not on implementation.

checklist.step: Feed results into the model monitoring plan
actions: Add the key fairness metrics for each tested model to the production monitoring dashboard with the same thresholds used in the test.
Set alerts to fire to the model owner and Model Risk Manager when a monthly metric crosses the investigation threshold between annual tests.
Add population drift monitoring on the features identified as disparity drivers.
Confirm alert routing by triggering a test alert and recording who received it.
checklist.done: fairness metrics and drift on driver features are monitored in production with alerts proven to route to named owners.

checklist.step: File the evidence and set the next test date
actions: File the specification, snapshot id, notebook, results, decision memo and sign-offs in the compliance evidence repository under Conduct / ICP 19 against the model id.
Apply the 7-year-from-retirement retention label so a supervisor can be answered after decommission.
Write the test date and result back to the model record and set the next due date at 12 months, or earlier if remediation demands it.
Update the jurisdiction obligation calendar where a result must be reported, such as a Colorado quantitative testing submission.
checklist.done: the full test pack is filed under retention, the model record carries the result and next due date, and reporting obligations are calendared.

testing.step: Build the population of models that required a bias test in the period
actions: Extract every tier 1 and tier 2 model with its production version history and last bias test date.
Derive which models became due through the 12-month anniversary and which through a material retrain or threshold change, using the deployment history rather than the model record.
List models that were due and have no completed test as automatic exceptions before sampling.
Sign the population as complete with the extraction queries attached.
testing.done: the due-for-test population is derived from deployment history and every untested due model is already an exception.

testing.step: Reconcile completed tests to production model versions
actions: Match each completed bias test to the model version that was actually in production during the test window.
Flag tests run on a development version, a sandbox dataset, or a version superseded before the test finished.
Confirm the tested decision matches the decision the model drives in production, including the threshold in force.
Treat a test on the wrong version or the wrong threshold as no test at all.
testing.done: every completed test is tied to the production version and threshold it purports to cover, with mismatches listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of tests whose results breached a threshold and 100% of tier 1 models operating in Colorado, New York or the EU.
Add 8 tests drawn at random with a recorded seed from the remainder, minimum 15 tests in total.
Record population size, seed, draw date and stratification in the workpaper.
Where fewer than 15 tests exist, test the population in full and state that.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers every breaching test and every strict-jurisdiction tier 1 model.

testing.step: Re-run the metric computation from the archived snapshot
actions: Open the dataset snapshot id cited in each sampled report and confirm the snapshot still exists and matches the recorded row count.
Recompute the disparate impact ratio, approval-rate gap and standardized mean difference independently, without running the team's notebook.
Compare your figures to the report and treat any difference beyond rounding as an exception.
Confirm declines, referrals and non-take-ups are present in the snapshot rather than filtered out.
testing.done: headline metrics are independently recomputed from the archived snapshot and adverse outcomes are proven present in the population.

testing.step: Test the proxy methodology and its match rate
actions: Confirm the BIFSG reference data vintage used and that the geocoding match rate is stated in the report.
Recompute the match rate from the proxy assignment file and check that unmatched records were excluded rather than defaulted to a group.
Verify the proxy table sits under restricted access and was not written back to any operational or underwriting record.
Flag any test whose match rate is low enough to make group-level conclusions unreliable and where that limitation is not disclosed in the report.
testing.done: the proxy vintage, match rate and access controls are verified and undisclosed reliability limitations are flagged.

testing.step: Confirm thresholds were fixed before results were seen
actions: Pull the version history of each sampled test specification from the repository.
Confirm the Model Risk Manager signature on the metric and threshold section pre-dates the first computed result.
Flag any specification amended after results were produced and read the amendment to see whether a threshold moved.
Treat a post-hoc threshold change as an exception regardless of the technical merit argued for it.
testing.done: each specification's threshold section is proven signed before results existed, with every post-hoc amendment flagged.

testing.step: Re-perform the conditional analysis and challenge the controls
actions: Refit the outcome model on the sampled snapshot with the controls the report claims, and compare the residual group effect to the reported figure.
Test each control variable for its own association with the group indicator and challenge any that behaves as a proxy.
Check each control is genuinely a filed or documented rating or underwriting factor, not an ad hoc addition that absorbed the disparity.
Report where removing a questionable control changes the conclusion.
testing.done: the conditional result is reproduced, every control is verified as legitimate, and control-sensitivity of the conclusion is reported.

testing.step: Trace remediation decisions to real, retested change
actions: For each breaching test, open the GRC issue and confirm a dated remediation decision, an implementation date and a retest date exist.
Confirm the implementation actually reached production by checking the deployment or configuration change record.
Confirm the retest ran on post-remediation decisions and that the issue was closed on the retest result, not on implementation.
For models kept running under a breach, confirm the Chief Risk Officer signature and that the named compensating control is configured and operating.
testing.done: every breach traces to an implemented change, a post-change retest and, where relevant, a signed and operating compensating control.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying model id, version, jurisdiction, the metric involved and the consumer group affected.
Assign a root cause from the standing list (test skipped, wrong version tested, threshold moved after results, adverse outcomes filtered out, remediation not retested) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require immediate escalation to the Chief Risk Officer for any model released with an unexplained breach.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time bias-test completion rate, the count of breaches unresolved beyond 90 days and the metric re-performance difference rate.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who built or tested none of the sampled models, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any model running under an unresolved breach to the AI Governance Committee and the board risk committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states completion rate, unresolved breaches, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, and is filed.

checklist.step: Set the annual review scope and calendar
actions: List every document in the AI governance programme with its current version, approval date and review due date from the GRC policy register.
Set the review window so board approval lands before the anniversary of the last approval, working back at least 10 weeks for drafting, consultation and committee slots.
Book the AI Governance Committee and board risk committee agenda slots now and record the dates on each policy record.
Name a drafting owner and a reviewing owner for each document so no policy is reviewed only by its author.
checklist.done: each programme document has a review window, booked committee dates and separate drafting and reviewing owners.

checklist.step: Refresh the jurisdiction requirements map
actions: List every jurisdiction the group writes business in and record the AI-specific instrument in force: NAIC model bulletin adoption and its state effective date, Colorado Reg 10-1-1, NY DFS Circular Letter 7, EU AI Act obligations, plus the IAIS ICPs the group-wide supervisor applies.
For each instrument record the specific programme elements it demands — written programme, board oversight, risk tiering, testing, vendor controls, documentation, consumer disclosure.
Mark instruments adopted or amended since the last review and set a 60-day gap assessment task for each.
Publish the map to the AI Governance Committee with the changes highlighted.
checklist.done: the requirements map lists every jurisdiction's AI instrument, its demanded programme elements and a gap task for each change.

checklist.step: Run the gap assessment of the programme against the map
actions: Build a matrix with each demanded programme element down the side and each policy section across the top.
For every element record the policy section that satisfies it, or mark it a gap with the jurisdictions exposed.
Assess partial coverage honestly — an element mentioned but with no owner, control or evidence requirement is a gap, not coverage.
Rank gaps by jurisdictional exposure and consumer impact and give each a proposed drafting change.
checklist.done: every demanded element maps to a specific policy section or is a ranked gap with a proposed drafting change.

checklist.step: Pull the operating evidence that shows how the programme actually ran
actions: Collect the year's operating data: models registered and retired, risk-tier distribution, validations and bias tests completed on time, shadow models found, AI-related consumer complaints and AI incidents.
Pull the exception register and summarise exceptions by policy and by root cause.
Collect the AI Governance Committee minutes and list the decisions taken and the items that stayed open more than two meetings.
Write a one-page operating summary that says where the written programme and actual practice diverged.
checklist.done: a one-page operating summary evidences how the programme ran and names every point where practice diverged from the text.

checklist.step: Draft the programme changes
actions: Redline each document against the gap list and the operating summary, changing the text to match either the requirement or the workable practice, never leaving both wrong.
Make every control statement testable: name the performing role, the frequency, the evidence produced and where it is filed.
Update the roles and responsibilities section against the current organisation chart and remove roles that no longer exist.
Keep a change log at the front of each document listing what changed and why.
checklist.done: each document carries a redline, testable control statements with named roles and evidence, and a front-page change log.

checklist.step: Consult the functions that have to operate the programme
actions: Circulate the redlines to Data Science, Model Risk, Underwriting, Claims, Privacy, Procurement, IT Security and Internal Audit with a two-week comment window.
Hold a working session on any control the operating functions say they cannot perform at the stated frequency.
Record every comment with its disposition — accepted, amended, rejected with reason — in a consultation log.
Never quietly drop a control because it is inconvenient; escalate the conflict to the AI Governance Committee instead.
checklist.done: a consultation log records every comment and its disposition, with unresolved control conflicts escalated rather than dropped.

checklist.step: Take legal and privacy clearance
actions: Read the drafts against the jurisdiction requirements map and confirm the wording does not promise more or less than the instruments demand.
Confirm with the Data Protection Officer that the data provisions align to the privacy notices, lawful bases and retention schedules actually in force.
Confirm the consumer-facing commitments in the programme match what the disclosure and complaint processes can deliver.
Give written clearance on the file or return specific wording changes.
checklist.done: counsel and privacy clearance is recorded in writing, with programme commitments aligned to notices and complaint handling.

checklist.step: Recommend the programme through the AI Governance Committee
actions: Table the redlines, gap assessment, operating summary and consultation log as one pack.
Walk the committee through the material changes, the residual gaps and the resourcing each control needs.
Take a recorded recommendation to the board risk committee, or send items back with named owners and dates where the committee is not satisfied.
Record the minute reference against every document in the GRC policy register.
checklist.done: the committee has recommended the pack with a minute reference recorded against each document, or returned items with owners.

checklist.step: Obtain board or board risk committee approval
actions: Load the programme pack to the board portal at least five business days before the meeting.
Ensure the paper states plainly what the board is being asked to approve and what oversight it is accepting under ICP 7.
Capture the approval resolution in the minutes with the document versions and the approval date named.
Issue the minute extract to the Head of Compliance for filing against each policy record.
checklist.done: board approval of the named document versions is minuted and the extract is filed against every policy record.

checklist.step: Publish the approved versions and retire the old ones
actions: Publish the approved versions in the policy register with effective date, version number and the next review due date set at 12 months.
Archive superseded versions so they remain retrievable, and remove them from the live intranet and any team site copies.
Sweep SharePoint and team channels for uncontrolled copies and replace them with links to the register.
Announce the changes to all in-scope staff with a plain summary of what is different.
checklist.done: only the approved versions are live, superseded versions are archived and retrievable, and uncontrolled copies are removed.

checklist.step: Deploy role-based training on the changes
actions: Define the in-scope audience by role: model developers, model owners, underwriters and claims handlers using model output, procurement, and the AI Governance Committee.
Build differentiated modules — developers get lifecycle controls and documentation, front-line users get human oversight duties and adverse-action handling, procurement gets vendor AI due diligence.
Assign with a 30-day completion deadline, automated reminders at day 14 and day 25, and line-manager escalation after the deadline.
Report completion by role weekly to the Head of Compliance until the 95% threshold is met.
checklist.done: role-based modules are assigned with a 30-day deadline and completion is tracked by role to the 95% threshold.

checklist.step: Operate the policy exception process
actions: Require any deviation from the programme to be requested in advance with the business reason, the control not being met and the consumer risk created.
Require a named compensating control and an expiry date of no more than 12 months on every exception.
Route approvals by risk: Model Risk Manager for tier 2 and 3, Chief Risk Officer for anything touching tier 1 or consumer-facing decisions.
Report the open exception population and its ageing to the AI Governance Committee each quarter.
checklist.done: every exception is pre-approved at the right level with a compensating control and an expiry, and the population is reported quarterly.

checklist.step: Monitor regulatory change between annual reviews
actions: Subscribe to the NAIC bulletin adoption tracker, state DOI bulletin feeds, EIOPA and national supervisor publications, and the IAIS consultation and adopted-paper feed.
Triage each item within 5 business days into no impact, monitor, or gap assessment required, and record the reasoning.
Open a 60-day gap assessment task for every adopted instrument that touches AI use by insurers, and an out-of-cycle programme amendment where the gap cannot wait for the annual review.
Report the change backlog and its ageing to the AI Governance Committee each quarter.
checklist.done: every AI regulatory change is triaged within 5 business days and adopted instruments have a 60-day gap assessment task.

checklist.step: Report programme effectiveness to the board
actions: Build the annual effectiveness report: policy currency, training completion, exception ageing, gap closure, model inventory coverage, bias testing completion and AI incidents and complaints.
State plainly whether the programme is operating as written and name the areas where it is not.
Table it at the board risk committee alongside the approval of the refreshed programme and record the minute reference.
File the report and the minute extract in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: an annual effectiveness report with a plain operating conclusion is tabled and minuted at the board risk committee.

checklist.step: Retain the programme evidence set
actions: File each approved version with its board minute extract, gap assessment, consultation log and training completion extract under AI Governance / ICP 7.
Apply the 7-year-from-supersession retention label to every version so a supervisor can be shown what was in force on any past date.
Confirm the repository index allows retrieval by document, version, effective date and jurisdiction.
Run a retrieval test once a year by asking for the version in force on a random past date and timing the answer.
checklist.done: every version is filed under a 7-year retention label and an annual retrieval test proves point-in-time versions can be produced.

testing.step: Build the population of programme documents and their versions
actions: Export every AI governance policy record with version history, effective dates, approval dates, approver and review due dates.
Cross-check against the AI Governance Committee and board minutes for the period to find documents referenced in minutes but absent from the register.
List any document in force with no register record as an automatic exception.
Sign the population as complete with the export date and query recorded.
testing.done: the document population reconciles to committee and board minutes, with unregistered in-force documents already exceptions.

testing.step: Reconcile approval evidence to the board record
actions: For each in-force version, open the minute the register cites and confirm the resolution names that document and that version.
Confirm the approval date on the register matches the meeting date, not the date the minute was written or the document published.
Flag any version published before its approval date or approved by a body without the delegated authority to do so.
Capture the minute extracts into the workpaper.
testing.done: every in-force version traces to a minuted resolution naming it, with publication-before-approval instances flagged.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of documents whose review due date fell in the period and 100% of documents amended out of cycle.
Add 10 exceptions from the exception register drawn at random with a recorded seed, plus 20 staff training assignments stratified across the in-scope roles.
Record population sizes, seed, draw date and stratification in the workpaper.
State where a population was tested in full because it was smaller than the sample size.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers every due and out-of-cycle document plus seeded exception and training selections.

testing.step: Recompute review timeliness against the due dates
actions: Recompute each document's review due date as 12 months from its previous approval date, from the approval record rather than the register field.
Compare the actual approval date to the recomputed due date and record days early or late per document.
Recompute the 60-day gap assessment deadline for each jurisdictional instrument adopted in the period and compare to the assessment completion date.
Treat a register due date that does not match the recomputed one as a control exception in its own right.
testing.done: review and gap-assessment deadlines are recomputed from source dates with days late recorded per document and instrument.

testing.step: Re-perform the gap assessment on a strict jurisdiction
actions: Pick the two most demanding instruments in force — typically the Colorado regulation and the EU AI Act obligations — and read them directly.
Build your own element list and map it to the current programme text without looking at the team's matrix first.
Compare to the recorded gap assessment and treat any element you find uncovered but the assessment marked covered as an exception.
Capture the instrument text you relied on, with its version date, into the workpaper.
testing.done: an independent element-by-element mapping exists for the strictest instruments with every coverage disagreement listed.

testing.step: Test that control statements are actually operable and evidenced
actions: Pick 12 control statements across the policy set and for each identify the named performing role, frequency and evidence artefact.
Ask the named role to produce the most recent instance of that evidence and note how long it took.
Flag every control whose named role does not recognise it, or where no evidence exists for the stated frequency.
Distinguish a written control that is not performed from one performed differently — both are exceptions but with different root causes.
testing.done: each sampled control statement is evidenced by a real artefact produced by its named role, or the failure mode is recorded.

testing.step: Test training completion and reach
actions: Extract the in-scope population from the HR system by role and compare it to the assigned population in the learning management system.
List in-scope staff with no assignment — a completion rate on the wrong denominator is worthless.
Recompute the completion rate within 30 days of assignment and compare it to the 95% threshold and to the figure reported to the committee.
For 10 sampled completions, confirm the module version matched the policy version in force at the time.
testing.done: the in-scope denominator is verified from HR, the 30-day completion rate is recomputed, and module-to-policy version alignment is checked.

testing.step: Test the exception register for authorisation and expiry
actions: For each sampled exception confirm the request pre-dates the deviation, names the control not met and states the consumer risk.
Confirm the approver's seniority matches the routing rule — Chief Risk Officer for tier 1 or consumer-facing deviations.
Recompute the expiry date and list every exception still operating past it.
Confirm the compensating control named in the approval is actually configured and operating, not merely described.
testing.done: every sampled exception is pre-approved at the right level, within its expiry, with its compensating control proven operating.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the document or control, the jurisdictions exposed and the period the gap ran.
Assign a root cause from the standing list (review missed, approval not minuted, control unperformable as written, training denominator wrong, exception expired unrenewed) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require an out-of-cycle amendment where a jurisdictional gap is open.
Carry every open issue into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute policy currency, on-time gap assessment rate, training completion and open expired exceptions against the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored and approved none of the sampled documents, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open jurisdictional gap to the board risk committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states currency, completion and gap metrics, a conclusion and the board reporting date, and is filed.
