checklist.step: Fix the model card template and its mandatory sections
actions: Define the mandatory sections: intended use and explicit out-of-scope uses, population the model was trained for, feature list with source and permissible-purpose basis, output and threshold, explanation method, reason-code set, human oversight design, monitoring plan, known limitations and retirement triggers.
Make each section machine-checkable so the release gate can test completeness rather than presence of a file.
Publish the template with a worked example for a pricing model, an underwriting model and a claims triage model.
Version the template and record which template version each card was authored against.
checklist.done: a versioned, machine-checkable card template with worked examples per model type is published in the repository.

checklist.step: Write the intended use and out-of-scope statement
actions: State the exact decision the model informs, the product, the channel and the jurisdictions it is approved for.
State the out-of-scope uses explicitly — for example a model built for renewal pricing must say it is not approved for new business or for claims handling.
State the population the model was trained on and where the production population differs from it.
Sign the section as the accountable business owner, since misuse of a model is a business decision, not a technical one.
checklist.done: the card names the approved decision, product, channel and jurisdictions and lists explicit out-of-scope uses, signed by the business owner.

checklist.step: Document the feature list and each feature's permissible basis
actions: Export the feature list from the registered model version rather than transcribing it from a design document.
For each feature record the source system, the transformation applied, the refresh cadence and the lawful basis or permissible purpose for its use.
Mark any feature derived from consumer report data, and any feature previously flagged as a proxy in bias testing, with its status.
Flag features whose source is a vendor and link to the vendor's documentation.
checklist.done: the card's feature list is exported from the registered version with source, transformation, lawful basis and proxy status per feature.

checklist.step: Fix the explanation method appropriate to the model type
actions: Choose and document the method: coefficient and factor tables for a GLM, SHAP values for a gradient-boosted model, surrogate model or rule extraction for anything opaque.
State whether explanations are global (how the model behaves) or local (why this applicant got this score) and confirm a local method exists for any model driving an adverse decision.
Record the computation cost and latency of generating a local explanation so it is known whether it can run inline or must be batch.
Produce three worked local explanations from real scored records and attach them to the card.
checklist.done: the card names a local explanation method for every adverse-decision model, with three worked examples attached.

checklist.step: Map model drivers to consumer-facing reason codes
actions: Take the top contributing features from the explanation method and map each to a plain-language reason code the customer will actually receive.
Check each reason code says something the consumer can act on or verify, and reject codes that merely restate the score.
Confirm the code set covers the top four drivers for at least 95% of adverse decisions in a back-test, so a generic fallback is rarely used.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the wording meets the adverse-action and disclosure requirements of each jurisdiction the model serves.
checklist.done: every reason code maps to a model driver, is actionable in plain language and covers the top drivers for 95% of adverse decisions.

checklist.step: Design the human oversight for the model's risk tier
actions: For tier 1, require a named human decision-maker to review before any adverse action, with the model output presented as a recommendation plus its local explanation.
Define the referral triggers precisely — score bands, conflicting data, protected-class-adjacent edge cases, or any decision the model itself flags as low confidence.
Define the override authority: who can overturn the model, on what grounds, and how the override and its reason are recorded.
State what the reviewer must be shown on screen — inputs, score, top reasons, and the data the score relied on.
checklist.done: the card specifies the reviewer role, referral triggers, override authority and the exact information the reviewer must see.

checklist.step: Configure the oversight in the operating platform
actions: Build the referral queue and routing rules in the underwriting or claims platform to match the card's triggers exactly.
Surface the score, the top reason codes and the underlying values on the reviewer's decision screen rather than in a separate report.
Add the override reason field as mandatory and constrain it to a coded list plus free text.
Test the configuration end to end with three cases per trigger and record the evidence.
checklist.done: referral triggers, reviewer screens and mandatory override capture are configured and proven with three test cases per trigger.

checklist.step: Prove the human review is real, not nominal
actions: Measure median review dwell time on referred cases and the model-agreement rate for each reviewer.
Investigate reviewers whose agreement rate exceeds 98% or whose dwell time is under the time needed to read the screen — rubber-stamping defeats the control.
Sample 20 referred cases a month and confirm the reviewer's recorded rationale engages with the specific case facts.
Report the metrics to the Model Risk Manager monthly and feed persistent rubber-stamping into coaching or a design change.
checklist.done: dwell time, agreement rate and rationale quality are measured monthly with rubber-stamping identified and acted on.

checklist.step: Document the monitoring plan and its thresholds
actions: Record in the card the production metrics monitored: score distribution drift, feature drift on the top drivers, referral and override rates, performance against outcome, and fairness metrics.
Record the alert thresholds, the alert recipients and the action expected on each alert.
Confirm every metric in the card is actually implemented on the dashboard and fire a test alert to prove routing.
Link the dashboard from the card so a reader can move from documentation to live behaviour.
checklist.done: every monitoring metric in the card exists on a live dashboard with proven alert routing and a documented expected action.

checklist.step: State the known limitations honestly
actions: Record the segments where the model performs worst, with the supporting performance figures by segment.
Record data limitations — sparse segments, features with high missingness, vendor inputs that cannot be validated.
Record the conditions that would invalidate the model, such as a product redesign, a distribution shift or a change in the vendor score definition.
Give each limitation a mitigation or an explicit acceptance signed by the model owner.
checklist.done: limitations are stated with supporting figures and each carries a mitigation or a signed acceptance.

checklist.step: Review and sign the card before release
actions: Check every mandatory section is complete against the template version and that the feature list matches the registered model version.
Check the oversight design in the card matches the configuration evidence from the operating platform.
Check a local explanation can actually be produced for a randomly chosen recent record, in front of you.
Sign the card against the model version and date it, or return it with the specific sections that fail.
checklist.done: the card is signed against a named model version only after live proof that an explanation can be produced on demand.

checklist.step: Refresh the card on every material change
actions: Treat retrains, feature additions or removals, threshold moves and vendor input changes as material and open a card revision within 10 business days.
Re-export the feature list and re-run the worked explanations rather than carrying forward the old ones.
Record what changed and its expected effect on reason-code distribution and referral volumes.
Route the revision for Model Risk Manager signature before the new version reaches production.
checklist.done: every material change produces a revised, re-signed card with refreshed feature list and worked explanations before release.

checklist.step: Give consumers an explanation and a route to challenge
actions: Confirm the adverse decision letter or portal message carries the reason codes in plain language and names the data used.
Provide a stated route to request human review or correct the underlying data, with a service level for the response.
Log every such request as an AI-related contact so volumes and outcomes can be reported to the AI Governance Committee.
Feed repeated challenges on the same reason code back to the model owner as a documentation or model defect.
checklist.done: consumers receive plain-language reasons plus a working challenge route, and challenge volumes are logged and fed back.

checklist.step: Report documentation and oversight health to the committee
actions: Report each quarter: card completeness by tier, cards stale against the production version, referral and override rates by model, reviewer agreement outliers and consumer challenge volumes.
Name every tier 1 model running with an incomplete or stale card and the date it will be fixed.
Table at the AI Governance Committee and record the minute reference.
Escalate to the board risk committee any automated adverse decision path with no working explanation.
checklist.done: a quarterly pack reports card completeness and oversight metrics, with every stale tier 1 card named and dated.

checklist.step: Retain the documentation so past decisions stay explainable
actions: File every card version with its worked explanations, oversight configuration evidence and sign-offs under AI Governance / ICP 19 against the model id and version.
Apply the 7-year-from-retirement retention label so a decision made years ago can still be explained to a supervisor or a court.
Confirm the archived card is linked from the decision records the model produced, so a complaint file can reach the documentation.
Run an annual retrieval test: pick a real past adverse decision and produce the card, the reason codes and the reviewer record for it.
checklist.done: card versions are retained for 7 years from retirement and an annual retrieval test reproduces the documentation behind a real past decision.

testing.step: Build the population of production model versions and their cards
actions: Extract every model version promoted to production during the period from the registry and deployment history, with promotion dates.
Extract every model card version from the governance repository with its signature date and the model version it names.
Join the two and list production versions with no card and cards naming versions that never reached production.
Sign the population as complete with queries and extraction dates recorded.
testing.done: production versions and card versions are joined, with uncarded deployments and orphan cards listed before sampling.

testing.step: Reconcile card dates to deployment dates
actions: For each production version, compare the card signature date to the deployment date and record days before or after.
Flag every tier 1 deployment whose card was signed after go-live as a release-gate failure, not a documentation lag.
For material changes, recompute the 10-business-day refresh deadline and compare it to the actual card revision date.
Summarise the population as a compliance rate by tier.
testing.done: card-to-deployment timing is computed per version with post-deployment tier 1 cards flagged as gate failures.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of tier 1 production versions deployed in the half and 100% of versions where a card was signed after deployment.
Add 10 tier 2 versions drawn at random with a recorded seed, minimum 20 versions in total.
For each sampled version draw 15 adverse decisions it produced, stratified across referral and straight-through paths.
Record population sizes, seed, draw date and stratification in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all tier 1 versions plus seeded tier 2 versions and a stratified adverse-decision sample.

testing.step: Test card completeness against the template and the live model
actions: Check every mandatory section is present and substantive, rejecting placeholder text such as 'to be completed' or a single-line intended-use statement.
Compare the card's feature list to the feature list exported from the registered production version and list any difference.
Confirm the stated thresholds match the thresholds configured in the operating platform.
Treat a card that describes a different version of the model as no card for the version in production.
testing.done: each sampled card is complete and its features and thresholds match the live registered version, with differences listed.

testing.step: Re-perform a local explanation on a live record
actions: Pick a recent scored record for each sampled model and generate the local explanation using the method the card names.
Confirm the explanation runs, returns ranked drivers, and does so within the latency the card claims.
Compare the top drivers to the reason codes the consumer actually received for that decision.
Treat a documented method that cannot be executed on demand as an explainability failure.
testing.done: a local explanation is generated on demand for each sampled model and reconciled to the reason codes the consumer received.

testing.step: Trace sampled adverse decisions to reason codes and reviewer records
actions: Open each sampled adverse decision and read the reason codes sent to the customer against the drivers behind the score.
Confirm generic fallback codes were used on no more than 5% of the sample and investigate any that were.
Where the card's design requires human review, confirm a named reviewer, a timestamp and a case-specific rationale exist.
List every automated adverse decision that bypassed a required review as a conduct exception.
testing.done: each sampled adverse decision has traceable reason codes and, where required, an evidenced case-specific human review.

testing.step: Test the referral configuration against the documented triggers
actions: Read the card's referral triggers and independently query the decision population for cases meeting each trigger.
Compare the count that actually routed to the referral queue and list any trigger that silently fails to fire.
Recompute the referral rate and override rate per model and compare to the figures reported to the committee.
Test the override field for completeness and reject overrides recorded with a coded reason and no case-specific text where the design requires it.
testing.done: every documented trigger is proven to fire in production and referral and override rates are independently recomputed.

testing.step: Test reviewer behaviour for rubber-stamping
actions: Compute median dwell time and model-agreement rate per reviewer over the sampled period.
Identify reviewers above 98% agreement or below the minimum plausible dwell time and pull 10 of their cases each.
Read the recorded rationale on those cases and judge whether it engages with case facts or repeats a template.
Report rubber-stamping as a control failure of the oversight design, not merely an individual performance issue.
testing.done: reviewer dwell time and agreement outliers are identified and their rationale quality assessed on a case sample.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying model id and version, tier, the decisions affected and the consumer impact.

Assign a root cause from the standing list (card signed after deployment, card describes wrong version, explanation method not executable, trigger not configured, review bypassed, rubber-stamping) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require immediate suspension of automated adverse action where no working explanation or required review exists.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute tier 1 card compliance, the explanation re-performance success rate, the required-review bypass count and the fallback reason-code rate against the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no sampled card and built no sampled model, sign and date the workpaper.

Report the conclusion and any adverse-decision path lacking a working explanation to the AI Governance Committee and the board risk committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states card compliance, explanation and bypass metrics, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, and is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns every response to a supervisor's AI inquiry, data call, survey or attestation demand, and signs the attestations the group makes about its AI systems

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 9 (Supervisory Review and Reporting) on responding to supervisory requests with the IAIS Application Paper on the Supervision of Artificial Intelligence (2025) and ICP 19 on conduct; each response is also written against the requesting authority's own instrument — the NAIC AI/ML survey instructions, a state AI systems programme interrogatory, Colorado Reg 10-1-1 reporting, or an EIOPA questionnaire — read at intake

In-scope processes.value: Intake, clocking, evidence assembly, drafting, review, signature and submission of AI-related supervisory inquiries, data calls, surveys, market conduct interrogatories and periodic AI attestations, plus the follow-up cycle to closure

In-scope systems.value: Inquiry register holds the request, deadline clock, evidence pack and approvals; submissions go through the requesting authority's channel — SERFF for market conduct interrogatories, state portal or examiner secure email, NAIC survey portal, or the supervisor's own questionnaire tool

Compliance procedure documented.value: AI Supervisory Inquiry and Attestation Procedure — intake within 1 business day, scoping, evidence pull from the model inventory and bias test library, drafting, technical and legal review, officer signature, submission and closure

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Risk Officer and the AI Governance Committee; reviewed annually and after any inquiry that could not be answered from existing evidence

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Deadline is whatever the request states — market conduct interrogatories commonly 10 business days, data calls and surveys 30 to 60 days, annual attestations on a fixed calendar date; the register stores request date, receipt date, stated due date and an internal draft-ready date at due date minus 5 business days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Register alerts fire to the Head of Compliance and the Chief Data Officer at receipt and at due date minus 15, minus 5 and minus 2 business days, with daily escalation once overdue

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Request, scoping notes, the inventory and testing extracts relied on with their extraction dates, drafts, reviews, the signed response and the submission receipt retained 7 years from closure

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Late responses, answers later corrected, and any question the group could not evidence are logged with days late, the evidence gap exposed and the remediation that closes it

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs every late or corrected response and every remediation plan arising from an evidence gap the inquiry exposed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All AI-related supervisory requests and attestations in the period, taken from the inquiry register and reconciled to an independent sweep of the regulatory mailbox, portal message centres and market conduct exam files

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero missed stated due dates and zero unlogged requests; every quantitative statement in a response must be reproducible from a dated inventory or test extract; any attestation signed without documented evidence for each assertion is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven with fixed-date attestations; testing runs semi-annually across all requests received in the half, with 100% coverage of signed attestations

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Must not have drafted, reviewed, signed or submitted any sampled response or attestation

Evidence location for test results.value: AI supervisory response test workpaper (register extract, mailbox and portal sweep, sample, evidence re-performance, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Supervisory Correspondence / AI

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A complete file per request — the request, the response, the dated inventory and testing extracts behind every figure, reviews, signature and submission receipt — retrievable within 3 business days for a follow-up or an on-site exam

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager is the channel for conduct examiners and Regulatory Affairs Manager for prudential and group-wide supervisors; Regulatory Counsel clears any answer conceding a gap, a breach or an untested model

checklist.step: Intake the request and open a numbered file
actions: Sweep the regulatory mailbox, the SERFF market conduct message centre, state portal inboxes and the examiner correspondence channels each business day.

Register the request within one business day with authority, entity, request date, receipt date, stated due date, the instrument cited and the format demanded (free text, structured survey, spreadsheet template).
Attach the request and any template file, and assign a file number in the pattern AIQ-<entity>-<year>-<seq>.
Notify the Head of Compliance, Chief Data Officer and Regulatory Counsel the same day with the due date in the subject line.
checklist.done: the request is registered within one business day with authority, due date, required format and named owners, and the request attached.

checklist.step: Clock the deadline and set internal milestones
actions: Read the request for the response period and whether it runs in business or calendar days from the request date or the receipt date.
Compute the draft-ready date at due date minus 5 business days and the review-complete date at minus 2 business days.
Load all three dates into the register and switch on the minus-15, minus-5 and minus-2 alerts.
Where the period is unworkable, request an extension in writing before the halfway point and file the authority's reply.
checklist.done: the register holds the stated due date, both internal milestones and live alerts, with any extension evidenced in writing.

checklist.step: Decompose the request into answerable questions
actions: Number every question and sub-question exactly as the authority numbered them.
Tag each as inventory (which models exist), governance (what programme and controls), testing (bias and validation results), consumer (disclosures and complaints), or vendor (third-party models).
Identify for each the entity, product line, jurisdiction and period the authority is asking about, since a state examiner wants that state's business, not the group's.
Assign each tag group to its evidence owner — Chief Data Officer for inventory, Data Science Lead for testing, Market Conduct Manager for consumer questions, Third-Party Risk Manager for vendors.
checklist.done: a numbered question list exists with a tag, a scope and a named evidence owner per question.

checklist.step: Pull the inventory evidence for the exact scope asked
actions: Run the standing supervisory export filtered to the entity, jurisdiction, product line and period the request names.
Include model id, business use, decision affected, risk tier, deployment dates in the period, data sources, human oversight design and last validation and bias test dates.
Stamp the export with the extraction date and query so the figures can be reproduced later.
Reconcile the export count to the quarterly inventory snapshot for the same date and explain any difference before it is used.
checklist.done: a dated, query-stamped inventory export scoped exactly to the request is reconciled to the quarterly snapshot.

checklist.step: Pull the testing and validation evidence
actions: For every model in scope, pull the latest bias test report and independent validation report with their dates and the model versions covered.
Extract the specific metrics the authority asks for — disparate impact ratios, approval-rate gaps, methodology and proxy approach — rather than attaching whole reports where a figure is asked for.
List models in scope with no current test and state plainly why, since an omission the examiner finds later is far worse than a disclosed gap.
Record the dataset snapshot ids so every quoted figure can be re-run.
checklist.done: requested metrics are extracted per model with snapshot ids recorded and untested in-scope models explicitly listed.

checklist.step: Pull the governance and consumer evidence
actions: Extract the current AI governance programme version, its board approval minute reference and the training completion rate for the period.
Extract AI-related consumer complaints and challenge requests for the jurisdiction and period, with outcomes and cycle times.
Extract the open exception population touching in-scope models with approvers and expiry dates.
Assemble these into an evidence annex indexed to the question numbers.
checklist.done: a governance and consumer evidence annex is assembled and indexed to the numbered questions.

checklist.step: Draft the response in the authority's own format
actions: Use the authority's template or numbering exactly; where a spreadsheet template is supplied, populate it rather than answering in prose alongside it.
Answer each question directly first, then cite the evidence annex item and its extraction date.
Where the answer is 'no' or 'not yet', say so plainly and state what is being done and by when, rather than writing around it.
Keep every figure tied to a dated extract and never quote a number that exists only in the drafter's spreadsheet.
checklist.done: a draft in the authority's own format answers every numbered question with a direct answer and a dated evidence reference.

checklist.step: Run the technical accuracy review
actions: Trace every model count, tier count, metric and date in the draft back to the annex extract it cites.
Challenge characterisations that the evidence does not support, such as describing a model as human-reviewed where the referral rule does not cover every adverse path.
Confirm the scope filters used match the scope the authority asked for, particularly the jurisdiction filter.
Record the review with reviewer name, date and the changes required.
checklist.done: every figure and characterisation in the draft is traced to evidence by second-line review, with changes recorded.

checklist.step: Run the legal and privilege review
actions: Read for admissions of gaps, breaches or untested models and confirm the wording is accurate and deliberate.
Confirm no privileged advice, unrelated litigation material, personal data or vendor-confidential material is being disclosed without the right basis.
Check the answer against what the group has told other authorities on the same subject in the last 24 months using the register.
Give written clearance or return specific wording changes.
checklist.done: counsel has cleared the draft in writing with no unintended admission, privileged content or inconsistent prior statement.

checklist.step: Take officer signature on the response or attestation
actions: For an attestation, list each assertion being made and require the evidence reference for it to be on the file before signing.
Refuse to sign any assertion the evidence does not support and escalate the gap rather than qualifying the wording into meaninglessness.
Sign in the capacity the authority demands — some state AI attestations require an officer or the Chief Compliance Officer specifically.
Record signatory name, capacity and date on the register entry.
checklist.done: the response or attestation is signed in the demanded capacity with every assertion backed by a referenced evidence item.

checklist.step: Submit through the authority's channel and capture the receipt
actions: Submit through the channel the request names — SERFF market conduct correspondence for an interrogatory, the state portal or examiner secure email, or the survey tool for a data call.
Check file format, size and naming conventions against the instructions before uploading, and split oversized attachments in advance of the deadline.
Capture the confirmation number, submission timestamp and a screenshot of the submitted state into the file.
Update the register to Submitted with the actual date and compute days early or late.
checklist.done: the response is submitted through the specified channel with a captured confirmation and the register updated with the actual date.

checklist.step: Work the follow-up cycle to closure
actions: Log every follow-up question, examiner call and document request on the same file number with its own due date.
Prepare a written brief before any examiner interview covering the models in scope, their oversight design and the known gaps, and circulate a minute the same day.
Where the examiner requests a demonstration, arrange a live walkthrough of the referral queue and the explanation output rather than sending screenshots.
Ask in writing for confirmation of closure when the file has been quiet for 30 days.
checklist.done: every follow-up sits on the original file with its own due date and closure is confirmed or actively chased.

checklist.step: Convert exposed evidence gaps into remediation
actions: List every question the group could not answer from existing evidence and treat each as a control gap, not a drafting inconvenience.
Raise a GRC issue per gap with an owner, the control or artefact that must exist, and a due date before the next expected data call.
Report the gap list to the AI Governance Committee and track it monthly until closed.
Confirm closure with the evidence artefact itself, not with a status update.
checklist.done: each unanswerable question is a tracked issue closed only on production of the missing evidence artefact.

checklist.step: Pre-build the standing answers for recurring questions
actions: Maintain a question bank of the questions authorities repeatedly ask, with an approved answer, the evidence source and the refresh owner for each.
Refresh every standing answer quarterly against the current inventory, testing and programme evidence and date-stamp it.
Retire answers that no longer reflect practice rather than letting a stale answer be reused under deadline pressure.
Measure how much of each new request the bank covered and use that to decide what to add.
checklist.done: a quarterly-refreshed question bank exists with evidence sources and coverage of each new request measured.

checklist.step: Close and retain the file
actions: Confirm the file holds the request, question list, dated evidence extracts, drafts, both reviews, the signed response and the submission receipt.
Set the register status to Closed with the closure date and basis, and record any commitments made to the authority with their due dates.
Move the file under Supervisory Correspondence / AI with a 7-year-from-closure retention label.
Confirm retrieval by authority, entity, jurisdiction and subject.
checklist.done: a complete file is closed, filed under a 7-year retention label and retrievable by authority, entity and subject.

testing.step: Build the population of AI-related supervisory requests
actions: Export every AI-tagged register entry for the period with authority, entity, request date, due date, submission date and status.
Sweep independently: the regulatory mailbox, SERFF market conduct correspondence, state portal message centres and the market conduct exam files opened in the period.
List requests found in the sweep but missing from the register as automatic exceptions.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete.
testing.done: the register population is reconciled to an independent sweep of mailboxes, portals and exam files, with unlogged requests as exceptions.

testing.step: Reconcile submissions to the authorities' own records
actions: Open the correspondence history for each supervised entity in SERFF and the state portals and list inbound and outbound items for the period.
Match each outbound item to a register file number and a signed response on file.
Investigate any submission sent with no register entry or no recorded signature as a process bypass.
Record inbound and outbound counts per authority in the workpaper.
testing.done: portal correspondence reconciles item for item to the register, with every bypass investigated and written up.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of signed attestations and 100% of responses submitted after their due date.
Add 10 requests drawn at random with a recorded seed from the remainder, minimum 18 files in total.
Include at least one market conduct interrogatory and one structured data call so both formats are covered.
Record population size, seed, draw date and stratification in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers every attestation and late response plus both request formats.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths from the requests themselves
actions: Read the response period from each request, noting business versus calendar days and the start date it runs from.
Recompute the due date and compare to the register value; a wrongly clocked deadline is an exception even where the answer was timely.
Compute days early or late and compare to the register figure.
Confirm every claimed extension has a written authority reply dated before the original due date.
testing.done: due dates and days-late are recomputed from the requests, with clocking errors and unevidenced extensions listed.

testing.step: Re-perform the quantitative answers from the cited extracts
actions: For each sampled response, re-run the inventory export using the scope filters the response claims and compare model counts by tier and business use.
Re-pull two quoted testing metrics from the cited bias test snapshot ids and compare them to the figures in the response.
Check the scope filter actually matches what the authority asked for, particularly jurisdiction and period.
Treat any figure that cannot be reproduced, or a scope filter narrower than the question, as a fail.
testing.done: model counts and quoted metrics are reproduced from the cited extracts under the correct scope for each sampled response.

testing.step: Test attestations assertion by assertion
actions: List every assertion in each sampled attestation as a separate line.
Demand the evidence reference for each and open it — an assertion supported by a policy that says the control should happen is not evidence the control happened.
Confirm the signature capacity matches what the authority required and that the signature date follows the evidence dates.
Treat any unsupported assertion as a fail regardless of whether it happens to be true.
testing.done: every assertion in each sampled attestation is matched to operating evidence dated before the signature.

testing.step: Test completeness of the answers against the requests
actions: Build your own numbered question list from each sampled request without looking at the team's decomposition.
Map each question to the part of the response that answers it and flag any answered only with programme narrative where evidence was asked for.
Check that questions with a 'no' or 'not yet' answer were answered plainly rather than avoided.
List every gap with the request's own question number.
testing.done: every question in each sampled request maps to a substantive answer, or the gap is listed by question number.

testing.step: Trace exposed gaps and commitments through to closure
actions: List the commitments made to authorities in each sampled response and match them to GRC issues with owners and due dates.
Confirm each closed issue is closed on the evidence artefact the commitment promised, not on a status update.
Check whether gaps disclosed in one response were still open when a later response to another authority was sent, and whether that was disclosed.
Flag any commitment past its due date with no communication to the authority.
testing.done: every commitment to an authority traces to a tracked issue closed on a real artefact, with overdue commitments flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying file number, authority, entity, the control that failed and the regulatory consequence.

Assign a root cause from the standing list (request never registered, deadline miscalculated, figure not reproducible, assertion unsupported, wrong scope filter, submitted outside the process) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; require a written correction to the authority where a submitted figure was wrong.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and, where a figure was wrong, a correction to the authority.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time response rate, the unlogged-request count, the figure-reproduction rate and the unsupported-assertion count against the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, reviewed or signed none of the sampled files, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any unsupported attestation to the AI Governance Committee and the board audit committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states response, reproduction and assertion metrics, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, and is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the disclosure inventory and the build of required notices into forms, letters and portal screens on every product or process change

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 19 (Conduct of Business) Standards on pre-sale and point-of-sale information and ongoing disclosure, with ICP 18 on intermediary disclosure and the IAIS Application Paper on the Supervision of Artificial Intelligence (2025) for automated-decision notices; each notice is also written against the jurisdiction rule that mandates it (state form filing statutes, adverse-action requirements, privacy notice rules, EU IDD/PRIIPs equivalents) and re-read at each change

In-scope processes.value: Product and process change intake through to implementation: identifying which notices and disclosures a change triggers, drafting them, filing where required, building them into forms, letters, portal screens and scripts, and proving delivery

In-scope systems.value: Forms and correspondence are configured in the policy administration system's document composition, with templates held in the document management repository and filed versions tracked in SERFF

Compliance procedure documented.value: Disclosure Build Procedure — trigger matrix by change type and jurisdiction, drafting and plain-language standard, filing determination handoff, configuration and test scripts, delivery proof and the disclosure inventory refresh

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and Regulatory Counsel; reviewed annually and on any bulletin or model act change affecting required notices

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change — the disclosure must be built, tested and (where the form requires filing) approved before the change's effective date; prior-approval jurisdictions drive the latest submission date back off that effective date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Change record milestones alert the Policy Forms Specialist and Product Filing Specialist at T-90, T-60 and T-30 days to the target effective date, and the release gate blocks go-live where a required notice is unbuilt or unfiled

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Disclosure inventory entries, approved notice text with version and edition date, filing approvals, configuration test evidence and delivery proofs retained 7 years from withdrawal of the form

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any change that went live with a required notice missing, unfiled or undelivered is logged with the affected policy count, the jurisdictions exposed and the remediation mailing

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs every decision that a notice is not required, and every remediation plan where policyholders received a policy without a mandated disclosure

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All product, form, rate, rule and correspondence changes implemented in the period, and for each, the notices they should have triggered plus a sample of issued policy and correspondence packets actually delivered to customers

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any required notice missing from a delivered packet, delivered in the wrong jurisdiction version, or used before its filing approval is a fail; the disclosure inventory must show 100% of live notices with a current edition date and jurisdiction mapping

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change; testing runs quarterly over that quarter's implemented changes plus a delivered-packet sample, with 100% review of changes in prior-approval jurisdictions

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Must not have drafted, configured or approved any sampled notice build

Evidence location for test results.value: Disclosure build test workpaper (change population, trigger re-performance, packet sample, delivery proof, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Conduct / ICP 19

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The disclosure inventory by jurisdiction and product with edition dates and SERFF tracking numbers, plus sample delivered packets, producible for a market conduct exam form-review request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns the exam form review; Product Filing Specialist supplies filing approvals; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission that a mandated notice was omitted before it is sent

checklist.step: Maintain the disclosure trigger matrix
actions: Build a matrix of change types down the side — new product, rate change, form revision, underwriting rule change, claims process change, introduction of an automated decision, vendor data source change — and jurisdictions across the top.

In each cell name the notices triggered: point-of-sale summary, replacement notice, free-look statement, privacy notice, adverse-action notice with reason codes, automated-decision notice, complaint routing information, producer compensation disclosure.
Cite for each the instrument that mandates it and the timing rule — at quote, at delivery, within 30 days, at renewal.
Review the matrix quarterly against the regulatory change feed and date-stamp each revision.
checklist.done: a cited, date-stamped trigger matrix maps every change type and jurisdiction to the notices and timing rules it triggers.

checklist.step: Screen every change against the matrix at intake
actions: Add a mandatory disclosure-screening field to the product change record that cannot be left blank at intake.
Record change type, affected products, jurisdictions, channels and effective date, and run them against the trigger matrix.
Output a triggered-notice list per jurisdiction onto the change record and assign a drafting owner to each line.
Route to the Policy Forms Specialist any change touching an automated decision, since those trigger notices that manual processes do not.
checklist.done: every change record carries a completed screening with a per-jurisdiction triggered-notice list and a drafting owner per line.

checklist.step: Draft or amend the notice text to the plain-language standard
actions: Draft against the mandated content elements one by one, keeping a checklist showing which sentence satisfies which element.
Meet the readability standard the jurisdiction sets — commonly a Flesch score of 40 to 50 for policy forms — and record the score achieved.
Assign a form number and edition date in the house convention and print both in the footer of every page.
Where a jurisdiction mandates specific wording, use it verbatim and mark it as non-editable in the template.
checklist.done: each notice has drafted text mapped element by element to the requirement, a recorded readability score and a form number with edition date.

checklist.step: Review the drafts for legal and conduct accuracy
actions: Read each draft against the instrument's required elements and confirm nothing mandated is missing and nothing added creates an unintended promise.
Confirm the automated-decision notice describes the actual decision the model drives and the review right the customer really has.
Confirm the complaint routing information names the correct regulator contact for the jurisdiction.
Give written approval per notice per jurisdiction, or return specific wording changes.
checklist.done: each notice carries a written counsel approval per jurisdiction with mandated elements verified present and accurate.

checklist.step: Run the filing determination on every new or amended form
actions: Hand each new or amended notice into the filing determination process with its form number, edition date and affected jurisdictions.
Where filing is required, submit through SERFF under the correct TOI with the cover letter and any readability certification the state demands.
Record the SERFF tracking number, submission date, review method and disposition against the notice in the disclosure inventory.
Block use of the form in prior-approval jurisdictions until an approval or a satisfied deemer is recorded.
checklist.done: every new or amended notice has a determination, a SERFF tracking number where filed, and a recorded earliest-use date per jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Configure the notice into document composition
actions: Build the template in document composition with the approved text, form number and edition date locked, and the variable fields bound to real policy data elements.
Configure the trigger rules so the notice attaches on the right event — quote, issue, endorsement, renewal, adverse decision — for the right jurisdiction and product only.
Configure jurisdiction-specific variants as separate templates rather than conditional text blocks where the wording is mandated.
Set the effective-date window on the template so the previous edition stops and the new one starts on the right day.
checklist.done: the notice is configured with locked mandated text, bound data fields, correct event triggers and a dated edition switchover.

checklist.step: Configure delivery across every channel the customer uses
actions: Build the notice into the digital journey at the same point it appears in the paper packet, not buried behind a link.
Configure the e-delivery consent check so a customer without consent still receives the notice on paper.
Update agent-facing scripts and the broker portal packet so intermediary-delivered business carries the same notice.
Record which channels were updated and the release that carried each change.
checklist.done: the notice is live in digital, paper and intermediary channels with e-delivery consent handled and releases recorded.

checklist.step: Test the build before release
actions: Write test cases covering each triggering event by jurisdiction and product, plus negative cases where the notice must not appear.
Generate real document output for each case and read the rendered PDF for the correct edition date, complete text, correct merge values and no truncation.
Test the adverse-decision path end to end so the notice carries the actual reason codes produced for that case.
Log defects against the release and re-test; do not accept a screenshot of the template as evidence the document renders.
checklist.done: every triggering and non-triggering case has a rendered document reviewed for edition, content and merge accuracy, with defects retested.

checklist.step: Gate the release on disclosure readiness
actions: Add a release checklist item that every triggered notice on the change record is approved, filed where required, configured and tested.
Block go-live in any jurisdiction where a required notice is unapproved or unfiled, jurisdiction by jurisdiction rather than for the whole release.
Require a named Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager sign-off to release with any open disclosure item, with an expiry date.
Record the gate decision and its evidence against the release.
checklist.done: no jurisdiction goes live with an unapproved, unfiled or untested notice unless a named, expiring sign-off exists.

checklist.step: Update the disclosure inventory as the record of truth
actions: Add or update one inventory row per notice per jurisdiction per product: form number, edition date, triggering event, timing rule, mandating instrument, filing status and SERFF tracking number, template id and channels.
Retire superseded editions with their end date so it is always clear which edition was in use on any past day.
Link each row to the approved text, the counsel approval and the test evidence.
Reconcile the inventory to the templates actually active in document composition each quarter.
checklist.done: the inventory holds a complete, linked row per notice per jurisdiction with dated edition switchovers reconciled to live templates.

checklist.step: Prove delivery, not just generation
actions: Confirm every generated notice is archived to the policy document repository against the policy number with a generation timestamp.
Capture the delivery event — print and mail confirmation from the print vendor, e-delivery send and open records, or portal posting timestamp.
Run a weekly exception report of policies issued with no archived copy of a required notice and work it to zero.
Retain the rendered document itself, not just a record that it was produced.
checklist.done: every required notice is archived against the policy with a delivery event captured and the weekly missing-notice report worked to zero.

checklist.step: Train the front line on what changed
actions: Brief contact centre, underwriting and claims staff on the new or changed notice, when it goes out and what questions it will generate.
Update call scripts and knowledge base articles with the notice text and the approved answers to likely questions.
Assign a short module with a 14-day completion deadline to the affected roles and track completion.
Brief the intermediary channel through the Agency Relations Manager so producers deliver the current edition.
checklist.done: front-line and intermediary channels are briefed, scripts and knowledge articles are updated and module completion is tracked.

checklist.step: Monitor complaints and calls for disclosure failures
actions: Tag complaints and contacts that allege a missing, late, confusing or contradictory disclosure with a dedicated reason code.
Review the tagged population monthly for clusters by product, jurisdiction, channel and edition date.
Open a defect against the disclosure build where a cluster points at a configuration or wording problem rather than a one-off.
Report the tagged volumes and their root causes to the conduct committee each quarter.
checklist.done: disclosure-related complaints are separately coded, reviewed monthly for clusters and converted into build defects where systemic.

checklist.step: Remediate policyholders where a notice was missed
actions: Quantify the affected population by policy count, jurisdiction, product and the period the omission ran.
Decide the remediation with Regulatory Counsel: corrective mailing, reopened free-look or replacement window, or a rescission-rights notice, and set the mailing date.
Assess self-reporting obligations in each affected jurisdiction and record the decision and its basis.
Track the mailing to completion and retain the mailing file as evidence.
checklist.done: every omission has a quantified population, a counsel-agreed remediation executed to a mailing file and a recorded self-report decision.

checklist.step: Retain the disclosure evidence set
actions: File approved text, counsel approvals, filing approvals with SERFF tracking numbers, test evidence and inventory snapshots under Conduct / ICP 19 by product and edition date.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label so the record survives product sunset.
Confirm retrieval by form number, jurisdiction, product and date in force.
Run an annual retrieval test asking for the edition in force in a named jurisdiction on a random past date.
checklist.done: the disclosure evidence set is filed under a 7-year retention label and an annual test proves point-in-time editions can be retrieved.

testing.step: Build the population of implemented changes and issued packets
actions: Extract every product, form, rate, rule and correspondence change with an effective date in the quarter, by product and jurisdiction.
Add document composition template changes and correspondence releases so notice changes made outside the product change process are captured.
Extract the count of policies issued, renewed and adversely decided in the quarter by jurisdiction as the packet population.
Reconcile the change extract to the release notes and sign the population as complete.
testing.done: the change and packet populations are extracted, reconciled to release notes and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the disclosure inventory to live templates
actions: Export the active templates from document composition with their form numbers, edition dates and jurisdiction bindings.
Match each to a disclosure inventory row and list templates with no inventory row and inventory rows with no live template.
Compare edition dates on live templates to the edition dates the inventory claims are current.
Treat any live template whose edition the inventory does not know about as a control failure.
testing.done: live templates reconcile row for row to the inventory with edition-date differences and orphans listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of changes in prior-approval jurisdictions and 100% of changes introducing or altering an automated decision.
Add 20 changes drawn at random with a recorded seed from the remainder, minimum 30 changes in total.
Draw 40 issued or adversely decided policy packets stratified across jurisdiction, product and channel, including at least 10 adverse-decision packets.
Record population sizes, seed, draw date and stratification in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers prior-approval and automated-decision changes plus a stratified delivered-packet sample.

testing.step: Re-perform the trigger determination for each sampled change
actions: Read each sampled change and derive your own triggered-notice list from the instruments, without looking at the change record's screening.
Compare to the recorded list and treat any missed notice as an exception, including a notice correctly identified but for the wrong jurisdiction.
Check the timing rule recorded against the notice matches the instrument — at quote versus at delivery is a real difference.
Capture the instrument text relied on, with its version date, into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled change has an independently derived trigger list compared to the recorded screening with differences listed.

testing.step: Verify filing status and earliest-use dates in SERFF
actions: For each sampled notice requiring filing, search Filing Access on the recorded SERFF tracking number.
Confirm the filing exists for the right company, jurisdiction, TOI and form number and edition date.
Compare the disposition date to the date the template went live in document composition.
Treat any use of a form before its approval or satisfied deemer in a prior-approval jurisdiction as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every sampled filed notice traces to a real SERFF filing whose approval pre-dates the template's live date, or the breach is reported.

testing.step: Inspect delivered packets against the required notice set
actions: Open the archived packet for each sampled policy and list the documents it actually contains with their form numbers and edition dates.
Compare to the required notice set for that jurisdiction, product, channel and issue date from the inventory.
Flag missing notices, superseded editions, and notices from the wrong jurisdiction variant.
For adverse-decision packets, confirm the reason codes printed match the codes recorded on the decision.
testing.done: each sampled packet is compared document by document to the required set, with missing, stale and wrong-jurisdiction notices listed.

testing.step: Test delivery evidence, not just generation
actions: For each sampled packet, retrieve the delivery event — print vendor confirmation, e-delivery send record, or portal posting timestamp.
Confirm the delivery date meets the instrument's timing rule counted from the triggering event, recomputing the day count yourself.
For e-delivered packets, confirm valid e-delivery consent existed on the delivery date.
Treat a generated but undelivered notice as an omission.
testing.done: every sampled notice has a delivery event within the recomputed timing window with e-delivery consent verified.

testing.step: Re-run the build tests on a sample of configured templates
actions: In the test environment, generate documents for five triggering and three non-triggering scenarios per sampled template.
Read the rendered output for correct edition date, complete mandated text, accurate merge values and no truncation or overflow.
Confirm the mandated-wording blocks are locked and cannot be edited by a user in the composition tool.
Compare your results to the release test evidence and flag any case the original testing did not cover.
testing.done: sampled templates are re-tested on triggering and non-triggering scenarios with rendering, locking and coverage gaps recorded.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying change id or policy number, jurisdiction, product, the notice involved and the policyholder count exposed.

Assign a root cause from the standing list (trigger matrix stale, screening skipped at intake, filed but not configured, wrong jurisdiction variant, delivery failed, edition switchover mistimed) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where policyholders received a packet without a mandated notice, require a corrective mailing plan cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and, where policyholders were affected, a cleared corrective mailing plan.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the packet completeness rate, the count of forms used before approval and the trigger re-performance difference rate against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, configured or approved none of the sampled notices, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any pre-approval use and any corrective mailing to the conduct committee and the board audit committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states packet completeness, pre-approval use and trigger accuracy, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, and is filed.
